bulgarian: This stele was built after the reign of the Witch Queens... I wonder what they would make of it.

english: This stele has a unique resonance, but that's about all I've been able to puzzle out.
french: Cette stèle a une résonance qui lui est propre, mais c'est la seule chose que j'ai pu déceler.
russian: У этой стелы особая аура, но больше ничего я в ней пока не разгадала.
bulgarian: This stele has a unique resonance, but that's about all I've been able to puzzle out.

english: Was something hidden here?
french: Il y avait quelque chose de caché là-dedans ?
russian: Там было что-то запрятано?
bulgarian: Was something hidden here?

english: Hm. The surface is utterly seamless, but I sense this stele has a sealed compartment.
french: Mmm. La surface est bien lisse, mais je sens qu'il y a compartiment caché sur cette stèle.
russian: Хм. Поверхность абсолютно гладкая, но я чувствую, что в этой стеле есть потайной отдел.
bulgarian: Hm. The surface is utterly seamless, but I sense this stele has a sealed compartment.

english: There's a resonance that calls to me.
french: Elle fait résonner quelque chose en moi.
russian: Её аура как будто зовёт меня.
bulgarian: There's a resonance that calls to me.

english: I always come back to this stele.
french: Je viens souvent auprès de cette stèle.
russian: Я часто возвращаюсь к этой стеле.
bulgarian: I always come back to this stele.

english: After asking Louis to import this bathing suit, it would be disrespectful to not go to the Beach.
french: J'ai demandé à Louis de faire venir ce maillot de bain, alors ce serait lui manquer de respect que de ne pas aller à la plage avec.
russian: Раз уж я попросила Луи привезти этот купальник, было бы неуважением не пойти на пляж.
bulgarian: After asking Louis to import this bathing suit, it would be disrespectful to not go to the Beach.

english: I thought it was a little too modest at first...
french: Je le trouvais un petit peu trop sage, au début...
russian: Сначала он показался мне слишком скромным...
bulgarian: I thought it was a little too modest at first...

english: But it's grown on me.
french: Mais je l'aime bien au final.
russian: Но со временем я оценила.
bulgarian: But it's grown on me.

english: You know, Louis did an excellent job designing my swimsuit.
french: C'est Louis qui a conçu mon maillot, il a fait un excellent travail.
russian: Знаешь, Луи отлично справился с дизайном моего купальника.
bulgarian: You know, Louis did an excellent job designing my swimsuit.

english: Come in and wash the grime off, [Ari]. Please. You'll be doing all of us a favor.
french: Je t'en prie, entre donc te décrasser un peu, [Ari]. Tout le monde t'en sera reconnaissant.
russian: Заходи, смой с себя эту грязь, [Ari]. Пожалуйста. Всем нам станет легче.
bulgarian: Come in and wash the grime off, [Ari]. Please. You'll be doing all of us a favor.

english: I can't believe Taliferro would insult Dozy like that...
french: Je n'arrive pas à croire qu'il ait osé dire du mal de Dozy comme ça...
russian: Поверить не могу, что он смеет так оскорблять Дрёму...
bulgarian: I can't believe Taliferro would insult Dozy like that...

english: And even worse, he insulted my SHOES!
french: Et pire encore, de MES CHAUSSURES !
russian: И более того, он оскорбляет мою ОБУВЬ!
bulgarian: And even worse, he insulted my SHOES!

english: Taliferro was NOT nice about our $Bell Berry Bakewell Tart$.
french: Taliferro n'a pas été tendre avec notre $tarte aux clocherelles$.
russian: Талиферро СОВЕРШЕННО невежливо отозвался о нашем $тарте из колокольника$.
bulgarian: Taliferro was NOT nice about our $Bell Berry Bakewell Tart$.

english: Terithia always asks me to turn up the heat on the bath. Her capacity for high temperatures is impressive.
french: Terithia me demande toujours d'augmenter la température des bains. Sa résistance au chaud est impressionnante.
russian: Теризия всегда просит сделать воду погорячее. Её устойчивость к жару впечатляет.
bulgarian: Terithia always asks me to turn up the heat on the bath. Her capacity for high temperatures is impressive.

english: Actually, I fell asleep in there. Dozy had to fish me out...
french: Pour tout dire, je me suis endormie dedans. C'est Dozy qui est venu me repêcher...
russian: На самом деле, нет, я там заснула. Дрёме пришлось меня вылавливать...
bulgarian: Actually, I fell asleep in there. Dozy had to fish me out...

english: I think you'll find today's bath especially rejuvenating. I sure did.
french: Je pense que tu trouveras les bains particulièrement relaxants, aujourd'hui. En tout cas, c'est mon avis.
russian: Сегодняшняя ванна особенно бодрит. Сама в ней почти возродилась.
bulgarian: I think you'll find today's bath especially rejuvenating. I sure did.

english: Yes. Fine.
french: Bon. D'accord.
russian: Точно. В полном порядке.
bulgarian: Yes. Fine.

english: Hm.
french: Mmm.
russian: Хм.
bulgarian: Hm.

english: Did I leave the cauldron on? Well, I'm sure it's fine.
french: J'ai laissé le feu sous le chaudron ? Oh, ça devrait aller.
russian: Я точно убрала огонь под котлом? Ладно, уверена, всё в порядке.
bulgarian: Did I leave the cauldron on? Well, I'm sure it's fine.

english: Evening, [Ari]. I felt like chatting with the riffraff, so I was just heading to the Inn.
french: Bonsoir [Ari]. Je suis d'humeur à me mêler à la plèbe aujourd'hui, donc je suis en route pour l'auberge.
russian: Вечер добрый, [Ari]. Мне захотелось поболтать с простолюдинами, так что я направляюсь в трактир.
bulgarian: Evening, [Ari]. I felt like chatting with the riffraff, so I was just heading to the Inn.

english: Still, I wish Terithia lived a little closer to town.
french: Cela dit, j'aimerais bien que Terithia habite un peu plus près de la ville.
russian: Жаль, что Теризия живёт далеко от города.
bulgarian: Still, I wish Terithia lived a little closer to town.

english: Where I'm from, it's customary to seek out the wisdom of women older than yourself.
french: D'où je viens, il est d'usage de s'en remettre à la sagesse des femmes plus âgées que soi.
russian: У нас было принято обращаться за мудростью к женщинам постарше.
bulgarian: Where I'm from, it's customary to seek out the wisdom of women older than yourself.

english: Josephine's got someone new to fuss over.
french: Depuis que tu es là, Joséphine a une nouvelle personne à dorloter.
russian: Теперь у Джозефины появился кто-то новый, о ком можно заботиться.
bulgarian: Josephine's got someone new to fuss over.

english: Oh, it's the newcomer. I suppose I should be thankful, I was the newcomer until you arrived.
french: Tiens, <she>la petite nouvelle</she><he>le petit nouveau</he><they>læ petit·e nouvelle·au</they> du village. Je devrais te remercier. Jusqu'à ton arrivée, c'est moi qu'on traitait ainsi.
russian:
О, это же

новенькие

новенькаяновенькийновенькое. Ну, наверное стоит тебя поблагодарить. До твоего приезда новенькой здесь была я.
bulgarian: Oh, it's the newcomer. I suppose I should be thankful, I was the newcomer until you arrived.

english: "I wasn't expecting to spend my hottest years in this podunk town, but here I am."
french: « Je ne m'attendais pas à passer les plus belles années de ma vie dans ce bled paumé, mais c'est comme ça. »
russian:
«Не

ожидали

ожидалаожидаложидало провести свои лучшие годы в этой деревушке, но вот как сложилось».
bulgarian: "I wasn't expecting to spend my hottest years in this podunk town, but here I am."

english: Oh, just me? Hm.
french: Oh, je suis la seule à penser ça ? Mmm.
russian: А, это только я так думаю? Хм.
bulgarian: Oh, just me? Hm.

english: I know what you're thinking...
french: Je sais ce que tu te dis...
russian: Знаю, о чём ты думаешь...
bulgarian: I know what you're thinking...

english: I shudder to imagine.
french: J'en ai des frissons rien que d'y penser.
russian: Даже думать страшно.
bulgarian: I shudder to imagine.

english: It was a busy week... What would I do without the weekend?
french: La semaine a été chargée. Je ne sais pas ce que je ferais si les week-ends n'existaient pas.
russian: Неделя была напряжённой... Что бы я делала без выходных?
bulgarian: It was a busy week... What would I do without the weekend?

english: These ruins are part of what drew me to Mistria. There's not much left from the era of the Witch Queens... especially so intact.

french: Rien de tel qu'une =euphorbe= pour égayer une pièce.
russian: =Пуансеттии= замечательно подходят, чтобы добавить света в пространство.
bulgarian: There's nothing like a nice =Poinsettia= for brightening a room.

english: I hope you handled it carefully, they're quite poisonous.
french: J'espère que tu l'as manipulée avec précaution, elle est très toxique.
russian:
Надеюсь, ты

несли

несланёснесло его осторожно: он весьма ядовитый.
bulgarian: I hope you handled it carefully, they're quite poisonous.

english: A =Red Toadstool=! Thank you, [Ari].
french: Une =amanite tue-mouches= ! Merci, [Ari].
russian: А, =мухомор=! Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: A =Red Toadstool=! Thank you, [Ari].

english: =Red Wine=? I do like a glass of red.
french: Du =vin rouge= ? J'aime bien boire un verre de temps à autre.
russian: =Красное вино=? Да, не откажусь от бокальчика красного.
bulgarian: =Red Wine=? I do like a glass of red.

english: Thank you, [Ari]. This kind of flower suits me.
french: Merci, [Ari]. Ce genre de fleur me convient tout à fait.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]. Такой цветок мне подходит.
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]. This kind of flower suits me.

english: Ah, =Shadow Flower=.
french: Ah, une =pénombranthe=.
russian: А, =теневой цветок=.
bulgarian: Ah, =Shadow Flower=.

english: Smooth.
french: Pourquoi pas ?!
russian: Очаровательно.
bulgarian: Smooth.

english: You're giving dirt to the owner of the Bathhouse?
french: Tu offres une motte de terre à une femme qui dirige des bains ?
russian: Ты даришь хозяйке купальни землю?
bulgarian: You're giving dirt to the owner of the Bathhouse?

english: Well, I won't pry. Which means you shouldn't ask what spellwork I'll be using this fruit for.
french: Non, ne me dis pas ! En retour, ne me demande pas à quel sort ce fruit me servira.
russian: Ладно, не буду допытываться. А значит, и ты не будешь спрашивать, в какой магии я буду этот плод применять.
bulgarian: Well, I won't pry. Which means you shouldn't ask what spellwork I'll be using this fruit for.

english: Now where did you find a =Spell Fruit=?
french: Où donc as-tu trouvé un =amuse-papilles= ?
russian:
И где же ты

раздобыли

раздобылараздобылраздобыло =волшебный плод=?
bulgarian: Now where did you find a =Spell Fruit=?

english: While it does seem like a waste of a potential reagent for my work...
french: Bien que ce soit du gâchis d'utiliser ainsi un réactif potentiel pour mes travaux...
russian: Это, конечно, трата ценного ингредиента для моих опытов...
bulgarian: While it does seem like a waste of a potential reagent for my work...

english: I have heard that the flavor is simply magical.
french: Il paraît que son goût est magique.
russian: Но я слышала, что вкус у него совершенно волшебный.
bulgarian: I have heard that the flavor is simply magical.

english: So I suppose I'll need to savor it. Thanks, [Ari].
french: Je vais donc être obligée de le déguster. Merci, [Ari].
russian: Так что распробую его как следует. Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: So I suppose I'll need to savor it. Thanks, [Ari].

english: A =Spell Fruit Parfait=!
french: Un =parfait à l'amuse-papilles= !
russian: =Волшебное парфе=!
bulgarian: A =Spell Fruit Parfait=!

english: Thanks, [Ari].
french: Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari].

english: Ah, these =Toasted Sunflower Seeds= will make a fine snack.
french: Ah, ces =graines de tournesol grillées= feront un parfait encas.
russian: О, =жареные семечки= — хорошая закуска.
bulgarian: Ah, these =Toasted Sunflower Seeds= will make a fine snack.

english: I-
french: Je...
bulgarian: I-

english: Oh!
french: Oh !
russian: Ой!
bulgarian: Oh!

english: Thank you [Ari], I love it!
french: Merci, [Ari], je l'adore !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari], как раз его мне и не хватало!
bulgarian: Thank you [Ari], I love it!

english: W-what is this?
french: Que... Qu'est-ce que c'est ?
russian: Ч-что это?
bulgarian: W-what is this?

english: =Water Chestnut Fritters=! You have good taste, [Ari].
french: Des =beignets de châtaignes d'eau= ! Tu as bon goût, [Ari].
russian: =Жареные водяные орешки=! У тебя хороший вкус, [Ari].
bulgarian: =Water Chestnut Fritters=! You have good taste, [Ari].

english: I do like a glass of =White Wine=. And it would be rude to turn you down.
french: J'apprécie le =vin blanc=. Et ce serait grossier de le refuser.
russian: Да, я не против стаканчика =белого вина=. Да и потом, отказывать тебе было бы невежливо.
bulgarian: I do like a glass of =White Wine=. And it would be rude to turn you down.

english: I put the $Void Newt$ you gave me into my cauldron for safe keeping, but it seems to have slipped out when I wasn't looking.
french: J'ai placé le $triton du néant$ que tu m'as donné dans mon chaudron, par sécurité, mais il a dû s'échapper pendant que je regardais ailleurs.
russian:
Я положила $пустотного тритона$, что ты мне

дали

даладалдало, в свой котёл для хранения. Но, видимо, он выбрался, пока я не видела.
bulgarian: I put the $Void Newt$ you gave me into my cauldron for safe keeping, but it seems to have slipped out when I wasn't looking.

english: Strange...
french: Bizarre...
russian: Странно...
bulgarian: Strange...

english: Most sorceresses have an affinity for tea, but it's a =latte= for me. Darcy makes it perfect for me. Oh, and she draws something in the foam... that's important.
french: Les sorcières ont souvent un faible pour le thé. Moi, je suis plutôt =café latte=. Celui de Darcy est délicieux. Et, très important, elle fait des dessins dans la mousse.
russian: У большинства чародеек тяга к чаю, но я предпочитаю =латте=. Дарси готовит его идеально. И ещё рисует на пенке разное... А это важно.
bulgarian: Most sorceresses have an affinity for tea, but it's a =latte= for me. Darcy makes it perfect for me. Oh, and she draws something in the foam... that's important.

english: [Ari], look! Darcy drew Dozy in the foam of my latte! So... cute... I-It's too cute to drink...
french: [Ari], regarde ! Darcy a dessiné Dozy dans la mousse de mon café latte ! C'est trop mignon... J'hésite même à le boire.
russian: [Ari], смотри! Дарси нарисовала Дрёму на пенке моего латте! Такой... милый... Я... Я не могу это выпить...
bulgarian: [Ari], look! Darcy drew Dozy in the foam of my latte! So... cute... I-It's too cute to drink...

english: Darcy understands that I'm not picky, I just know what I like, and I like it exactly that way every time.
french: Darcy sait que je ne suis pas difficile. Je sais juste ce que je veux et comment je le veux à chaque fois.
russian: Дарси прекрасно понимает, что я не привередливая. Я просто знаю чего хочу, и хочу я это всегда строго определённым образом.
bulgarian: Darcy understands that I'm not picky, I just know what I like, and I like it exactly that way every time.

english: It was a pleasant surprise to find I have access to a good tailor out here in the country.
french: J'étais agréablement surprise quand j'ai su qu'il y avait un bon tailleur ici, à la campagne.
russian: Было приятно обнаружить, что даже в провинции есть толковый портной.
bulgarian: It was a pleasant surprise to find I have access to a good tailor out here in the country.

english: Louis makes boots that are to die for. The man is indispensable...
french: Louis fabrique des bottes à tomber par terre. C'est un homme précieux...
russian: Луи шьёт такие ботинки — умереть можно. Он просто незаменим...
bulgarian: Louis makes boots that are to die for. The man is indispensable...

english: Louis always respects my choice to raise a hemline and lower a neckline.
french: Louis respecte toujours mon choix de raccourcir le bas et d'échancrer au niveau du décolleté.
russian: Луи всегда уважает моё право поднять подол и опустить вырез.
bulgarian: Louis always respects my choice to raise a hemline and lower a neckline.

english: Poor Louis, exiled from the Capital... I can break a curse without breaking a sweat, but banishment is a whole other story.
french: Pauvre Louis, s'être fait bannir de la capitale... Je peux briser n'importe quelle malédiction, mais l'exil, c'est une autre paire de manches.
russian: Бедный Луи, изгнанный из столицы... Проклятие-то я могу снять без проблем, но с изгнанием всё сложнее.
bulgarian: Poor Louis, exiled from the Capital... I can break a curse without breaking a sweat, but banishment is a whole other story.

english: Merri loves me... she spent months restoring that circular bed, but no one was buying until I came along. There's even an ottoman for Dozy... how could I resist?
french: Merri m'adore. Elle avait passé des mois à restaurer ce lit circulaire, mais il ne trouvait pas preneur avant que j'arrive. Il y a même un pouf pour Dozy... Comment résister ?
russian: Мэрри меня обожает... она несколько месяцев реставрировала ту круглую кровать, но её никто не покупал... пока не пришла я. Даже пуф для Дрёмы был — как устоять?
bulgarian: Merri loves me... she spent months restoring that circular bed, but no one was buying until I came along. There's even an ottoman for Dozy... how could I resist?

english: Merri helped me furnish the Bathhouse very quickly after I arrived... she even managed to find me the perfect chair for my desk.
french: Merri m'a aidée à meubler les bains très rapidement après mon arrivée... Elle a même réussi à dégoter un siège parfaitement assorti au comptoir.
russian: Мэрри помогла обставить купальню сразу после моего приезда... Даже кресло нашла — идеальное для моего стола.
bulgarian: Merri helped me furnish the Bathhouse very quickly after I arrived... she even managed to find me the perfect chair for my desk.

english: Valen called it a "throne" the other day, can you imagine? If I had a throne it wouldn't be so understated!
french: L'autre fois, Valen a dit que c'était un « trône »... Si c'en était un, il ne serait pas aussi sobre !
russian: Вален на днях назвала его «троном», представляешь? Если бы у меня был трон, он точно был бы не таким скромным!
bulgarian: Valen called it a "throne" the other day, can you imagine? If I had a throne it wouldn't be so understated!

english: I have plenty of potion racks, but Merri's keeping an eye out for the vintage kind. Old things hold power, [Ari].
french: J'ai plein d'étagères pour mes potions, mais Merri essaie de m'en trouver d'époque. Les antiquités ont un certain pouvoir, [Ari].
russian: Полок для зелий у меня полно, но Мэрри ищет мне винтажные. Старые вещи хранят силу, [Ari].
bulgarian: I have plenty of potion racks, but Merri's keeping an eye out for the vintage kind. Old things hold power, [Ari].

english: Sometimes I'll see a piece at Merri's that doesn't speak to me... and then she'll show me the purple version... she sure knows how to make a sale.
french: Parfois, je vois un meuble qui ne me plaît pas plus que ça chez Merri... Puis elle me le montre en mauve... Elle connaît son métier.
russian: Иногда приглядываюсь у Мэрри к некоторым вещам, и они меня совсем не трогают... а потом Мэрри показывает фиолетовый вариант... Эта женщина умеет продавать.
bulgarian: Sometimes I'll see a piece at Merri's that doesn't speak to me... and then she'll show me the purple version... she sure knows how to make a sale.

english: Everything Stillwell says is technically true, but does he have to be so dramatic about it? He should be more like me... I've never been dramatic a day in my life.
bulgarian: Everything Stillwell says is technically true, but does he have to be so dramatic about it? He should be more like me... I've never been dramatic a day in my life.

english: Valen thinks I'm foolish for believing in Stillwell's fortunes, but he's never wrong. Though he is a bit vague, sometimes...
bulgarian: Valen thinks I'm foolish for believing in Stillwell's fortunes, but he's never wrong. Though he is a bit vague, sometimes...

english: Divine foresight... there are tales of that power in the tomes of the ancient Witch Queens, but I'd never want it myself. I mean, just look how gloomy Stillwell is. No thanks.
bulgarian: Divine foresight... there are tales of that power in the tomes of the ancient Witch Queens, but I'd never want it myself. I mean, just look how gloomy Stillwell is. No thanks.

english: "The torturous grind of time's wheel will rot the very grain of your existence"... is Stillwell talking about the sourdough in the back of my cupboard? That would explain the smell...
bulgarian: "The torturous grind of time's wheel will rot the very grain of your existence"... is Stillwell talking about the sourdough in the back of my cupboard? That would explain the smell...

english: He wouldn't appreciate a good meal if it hit him in the face!
french: Il ne saurait pas apprécier un plat digne de ce nom même si on lui mettait le nez dedans !
russian: Он не оценит блюдо по достоинству, даже если ему в лицо швырнуть!
bulgarian: He wouldn't appreciate a good meal if it hit him in the face!

english: Even if the side dishes hit him in the face too! And dessert also!
french: Et je ne parle même pas de l'entrée ! Ou du dessert !
russian: И гарнир швырнуть тоже! И все десерты!
bulgarian: Even if the side dishes hit him in the face too! And dessert also!

english: That Taliferro...
french: Ce Taliferro...
russian: Этот Талиферро...
bulgarian: That Taliferro...

english: With a new tongue, maybe he'd finally appreciate my cooking!
french: Avec une nouvelle langue, il finirait peut-être par apprécier ma cuisine !
russian: Может, с новым языком он, наконец, оценит мои кулинарные старания!
bulgarian: With a new tongue, maybe he'd finally appreciate my cooking!

english: Strictly between you and me, I'm thinking of turning Taliferro into a frog.
french: Ça reste entre nous, mais j'ai bien envie de transformer ce Taliferro en crapaud.
russian: Только между нами: я думаю превратить Талиферро в лягушку.
bulgarian: Strictly between you and me, I'm thinking of turning Taliferro into a frog.

english: Ah, my old nemesis... Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$.
french: Ah, mon pire cauchemar... Le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro.
russian: А, мой старый враг... $Смотр блюд$ Талиферро.
bulgarian: Ah, my old nemesis... Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$.

english: Some people think gorgeous, perfectly styled hair gives you a license to say whatever rude thing you want.
french: Certains s'imaginent qu'une coupe de cheveux impeccable les autorise à être désagréables.
russian: Некоторые люди считают, что шикарные, идеально уложенные волосы дают право говорить любые гадости.
bulgarian: Some people think gorgeous, perfectly styled hair gives you a license to say whatever rude thing you want.

english: Ugh, Taliferro.
french: Ah, Taliferro...
russian: Ух, Талиферро!
bulgarian: Ugh, Taliferro.

english: Maybe I should let Vera style my hair...
french: Je devrais peut-être demander à Vera de me coiffer...
russian: Может, стоит позволить Вере уложить мне волосы...
bulgarian: Maybe I should let Vera style my hair...

english: I've got a potion that turns skin blue, [Ari]. Because you'd suffocate if you drank it. It's a work in progress.
french: J'ai une potion qui teint les gens en bleu, [Ari]. En fait, ils sont bleus parce qu'ils étouffent. Je dois encore travailler dessus.
russian: У меня есть зелье, от которого кожа становится синей, [Ari]. Потому что, если его выпить, начнёшь задыхаться. Я работаю над этим.
bulgarian: I've got a potion that turns skin blue, [Ari]. Because you'd suffocate if you drank it. It's a work in progress.

english: Vera says she has a dye that turns hair blue... hah!
french: Vera dit qu'elle a une coloration qui teint les cheveux en bleu... Ha !
russian: Вера говорит, у неё есть краска, делающая волосы синими... ха!
bulgarian: Vera says she has a dye that turns hair blue... hah!

english: I just want to see what would happen.
french: Juste pour voir ce qu'il se passerait.
russian: Мне просто любопытно, что из этого выйдет.
bulgarian: I just want to see what would happen.

english: Do you think Vera would notice if I infused her hair dye with mana...?
french: Tu crois que Vera s'en apercevrait si je mettais du mana dans ses colorations...?
russian: Как думаешь, Вера заметит, если я подмешаю в её краску ману...?
bulgarian: Do you think Vera would notice if I infused her hair dye with mana...?

english: I can't get my hair dyed here... I prefer to use potions, so there's no telling what color it would come out.
french: Je ne peux pas me teindre les cheveux ici... Je préfère utiliser des potions. Impossible de savoir quelle couleur ça donnerait.
russian: Здесь мне не покраситься... Я предпочитаю зелья. С ними никогда не знаешь, какой цвет получится.
bulgarian: I can't get my hair dyed here... I prefer to use potions, so there's no telling what color it would come out.

english: Those garish colors! The deliberate pattern clashing! And his awful, oversized belt buckles!
french: Ces couleurs chatoyantes ! Ces motifs qui s'entrechoquent ! Et ces immondes boucles de ceinture trop grandes !
russian: Такие крикливые цвета! И нарочно несовпадающие узоры! И эти кошмарно огромные пряжки!
bulgarian: Those garish colors! The deliberate pattern clashing! And his awful, oversized belt buckles!

english: He looks just like a poisonous frog...
french: On dirait un crapaud venimeux...
russian: Он похож на ядовитую лягушку...
bulgarian: He looks just like a poisonous frog...

english: Oh ho ho ho!
french: Oh ho ho ho !
russian: О-хо-хо-хо!
bulgarian: Oh ho ho ho!

english: Much as it pains me to admit, I can't help but respect Wheedle's sense of fashion.
french: Même si ça me désole de l'admettre, j'apprécie les tenues de Wheedle.
russian: Мне больно это признавать, но чувство стиля у Хлюста я уважаю.
bulgarian: Much as it pains me to admit, I can't help but respect Wheedle's sense of fashion.

english: 'Cash is king' my left heel... he doesn't know just how valuable my concoctions are!
french: « De l'argent ou rien », crétin... Il n'a aucune idée de ce que valent mes mixtures !
russian: «Только наличные» — ну да, конечно! Он просто не знает цены моим зельям!
bulgarian: 'Cash is king' my left heel... he doesn't know just how valuable my concoctions are!

english: I tried to trade Wheedle one of my home-brewed tonics for a bottle of his $Snake Oil$, and he turned me down flat!
french: J'ai essayé d'échanger un de mes toniques contre une bouteille d'$huile de couleuvre$ avec Wheedle, mais il a refusé !
russian: Я хотела обменять у Хлюста один мой домашний бальзам на флакон его $змеиного масла$, а он категорически отказался!
bulgarian: I tried to trade Wheedle one of my home-brewed tonics for a bottle of his $Snake Oil$, and he turned me down flat!

english: Who doesn't love something that's a little deep-fried?
french: Et puis, tout est appétissant dès que c'est frit, non ?
russian: Кому может не понравиться прожарка во фритюре?
bulgarian: Who doesn't love something that's a little deep-fried?

english: Obviously I don't need a third-party enhancement, but Wheedle's $Fast Food$ does look enticing, doesn't it?
french: J'ai plutôt le palais fin, mais je dois avouer que l'$encas sur le pouce$ de Wheedle a l'air appétissant.
russian: Меня, конечно, не интересуют чужие ускоряющие эффекты, но $фастфуд$ Хлюста выглядит весьма заманчиво.
bulgarian: Obviously I don't need a third-party enhancement, but Wheedle's $Fast Food$ does look enticing, doesn't it?

english: The very gall of it!
french: Ce n'est même plus de l'audace, là !
russian: Какая беззастенчивая наглость!
bulgarian: The very gall of it!

english: Wheedle tried to sell me a fake potion! Me!
french: Wheedle a essayé de me vendre une fausse potion, à moi !
russian: Хлюст пытался продать мне поддельное зелье! Мне!
bulgarian: Wheedle tried to sell me a fake potion! Me!

english: Maybe I'll just get him both.
french: Je vais peut-être lui prendre les deux.
russian: На всякий случай возьму оба.
bulgarian: Maybe I'll just get him both.

english: Which genre of $Song Crystal$ do you think Dozy would prefer, "experimental jazz" or "thrash metal"?
french: D'après toi, quel $cristal musical$ plairait le plus à Dozy, « Jazz expérimental » ou « Trash metal » ?
russian: Как ты думаешь, какой жанр $поющих кристаллов$ больше понравится Дрёме: «экспериментальный джаз» или «трэш-метал»?
bulgarian: Which genre of $Song Crystal$ do you think Dozy would prefer, "experimental jazz" or "thrash metal"?

english: Maybe someday, my achievements will be worthy of it!
french: Peut-être qu'un jour, je réussirai à m'en montrer digne !
russian: Возможно, однажды мои заслуги будут достойны его!
bulgarian: Maybe someday, my achievements will be worthy of it!

english: Ohoho!
french: Oh ho ho !
russian: Охо-хо!
bulgarian: Ohoho!

english: You've impressed me, [Ari]. The =Ancient Royal Scepter= you turned over is a symbol of the Witch Queen's authority.
french: Tu m'impressionnes, [Ari]. Le =sceptre royal antique= que tu as donné au musée est le symbole de l'autorité de la Reine-sorcière.
russian:
Ты

впечатлили

впечатлилавпечатлилвпечатлило меня, [Ari]. Этот =древний королевский скипетр=, который ты

передали

передалапередалпередало музею, — символ власти королевы-ведьмы.
bulgarian: You've impressed me, [Ari]. The =Ancient Royal Scepter= you turned over is a symbol of the Witch Queen's authority.

english: Don't worry your head about it, if he follows my advice it'll keep that glow for another thousand years.
french: Ne te mets pas martel en tête. S'il suit mes conseils, elle conservera cette lueur pendant encore mille ans.
russian: Не утруждай себя размышлениями: если он последует моему совету, свет сохранится ещё тысячу лет.
bulgarian: Don't worry your head about it, if he follows my advice it'll keep that glow for another thousand years.

english: Errol had me in to consult on the $Ancient Stone Lantern$ you donated.
french: Errol m'a permis d'examiner la $lanterne en pierre antique$ dont tu as fait don.
russian:
