bulgarian: Dell was awake when I got up... she wasn't up all night, was she?

english: I don't know what Holt's worried about, Dell's a heavy sleeper. She always sleeps through when it's time to stock the shelves in the morning.
french: Je ne sais pas pourquoi Holt s'inquiète, Dell est une grosse dormeuse. Elle ne se réveille même pas le matin, quand on réapprovisionne les rayons.
russian: Не знаю, чего Хольт беспокоится: Делл спит как убитая. Даже когда надо раскладывать товар с утра.
bulgarian: I don't know what Holt's worried about, Dell's a heavy sleeper. She always sleeps through when it's time to stock the shelves in the morning.

english: A morning bath wakes me right up!
french: Un bon bain le matin me donne de l'énergie pour toute la journée !
russian: Утренняя ванна меня сразу бодрит!
bulgarian: A morning bath wakes me right up!

english: I'm so glad I got to sneak a bath in before my shift!
french: Je suis si contente d'avoir pu prendre un bain avant d'aller travailler !
russian: Так рада, что успела сбегать в купальню до начала смены!
bulgarian: I'm so glad I got to sneak a bath in before my shift!

english: We've got sugar, flour and rice... everything you need to jump into cooking!
french: Nous avons du sucre, de la farine, du riz... Tout ce qu'il faut pour se mettre aux fourneaux !
russian: У нас есть сахар, мука и рис... всё, чтобы сразу приступить к готовке!
bulgarian: We've got sugar, flour and rice... everything you need to jump into cooking!

english: I can't remember when my feet started aching after a long day at the shop. The years do catch up.
french: Ça fait déjà bien longtemps que j'ai mal aux pieds après une journée passée au magasin. C'est ça de vieillir.
russian: Не помню, когда ноги стали ныть после долгого дня в магазине. Годы берут своё.
bulgarian: I can't remember when my feet started aching after a long day at the shop. The years do catch up.

english: Welcome to Mistria. I'm Nora, I run the $General Store$ in town with my husband and our daughters.
french: Moi, c'est Nora. Je gère le $magasin général$ avec mon mari et nos filles.
russian: Я Нора. Мы с мужем и дочерьми управляем $универмагом$ в городе.
bulgarian: Welcome to Mistria. I'm Nora, I run the $General Store$ in town with my husband and our daughters.

english: I'm also head of the Chamber of Commerce and the $Saturday Market$...
french: Je suis aussi la présidente de la Chambre de commerce et je m'occupe du $marché du samedi$...
russian: Я также возглавляю Торговую палату и курирую $Субботний базар$...
bulgarian: I'm also head of the Chamber of Commerce and the $Saturday Market$...

english: Though unfortunately the $Saturday Market$ has been on hiatus since the earthquake caused the $bridge into town to collapse$.
french: Malheureusement, le tremblement de terre a causé l'$effondrement du pont$ et le $marché$ n'a pas pu reprendre.
russian: Хотя, к сожалению, $Субботний базар$ на паузе с тех пор, как землетрясение разрушило $мост в город$.
bulgarian: Though unfortunately the $Saturday Market$ has been on hiatus since the earthquake caused the $bridge into town to collapse$.

english: Balor is currently the only merchant that even attempts the trip these days. And he has to do it all on foot.
french: À l'heure actuelle, Balor est le seul marchand à faire le déplacement. Et à pied, en plus.
russian: Сейчас только Балор пытается добираться сюда, и то пешком.
bulgarian: Balor is currently the only merchant that even attempts the trip these days. And he has to do it all on foot.

english: Broken bridge? I think I can help!
french: Un pont qui s'est effondré ? Je dois pouvoir faire quelque chose !
russian: Сломанный мост? Думаю, я могу помочь!
bulgarian: Broken bridge? I think I can help!

english: What's the Saturday Market?
french: C'est quoi, le marché du samedi ?
russian: А что такое Субботний базар?
bulgarian: What's the Saturday Market?

english: Oh, right! Adeline did mention you'd be helping the town in exchange for the farm.
french: Mais oui ! Adeline a dit que tu aiderais notre petite ville en échange de la ferme.
russian:
Ах, да! Аделина говорила, что ты

будете помогать

будешь помогатьбудешь помогатьбудешь помогать городу в обмен на ферму.
bulgarian: Oh, right! Adeline did mention you'd be helping the town in exchange for the farm.

english: If the $broken bridge$ were repaired, all sorts of merchants could resume bringing their wares to town on Saturdays!
french: Si le $pont$ était remis en état, les marchands itinérants pourraient revenir vendre leurs produits ici, le samedi. Tu adorerais !
russian: Если $сломанный мост$ починить, торговцы снова смогут приезжать в город по субботам. Тебе точно понравится!
bulgarian: If the $broken bridge$ were repaired, all sorts of merchants could resume bringing their wares to town on Saturdays!

english: It used to be a weekly event in Mistria... All sorts of traveling merchants from around the Kingdom would stop here to sell their wares.
french: C'est un marché qui avait lieu une fois par semaine à Mistria... Des marchands itinérants de tout le royaume venaient ici vendre leurs produits.
russian: Раньше это было еженедельное событие в Мистрии... Торговцы со всего Королевства заезжали сюда продавать свои товары.
bulgarian: It used to be a weekly event in Mistria... All sorts of traveling merchants from around the Kingdom would stop here to sell their wares.

english: If the $broken bridge$ gets repaired, the $Saturday Market$ could resume!
french: Si le $pont$ était remis en état, le $marché du samedi$ pourrait reprendre. Tu adorerais !
russian: Если $сломанный мост$ восстановят, $Субботний базар$ снова заработает. Тебе точно понравится!
bulgarian: If the $broken bridge$ gets repaired, the $Saturday Market$ could resume!

english: Well, if you need anything in the way of seeds and supplies, please stop by the store.
french: Si tu as besoin de graines ou de provisions, n'hésite pas à passer nous voir au magasin.
russian: Как бы там ни было, если нужны семена или припасы — заходи в магазин в любое время.
bulgarian: Well, if you need anything in the way of seeds and supplies, please stop by the store.

english: Ah, you must be [Ari].
french: Ah, tu dois être [Ari] ! Bienvenue à Mistria.
russian: Ах, ты, должно быть, [Ari]! Добро пожаловать в Мистрию.
bulgarian: Ah, you must be [Ari].

english: Sales always go down during a heat wave.
french: On fait toujours moins de ventes quand il fait chaud.
russian: Во время жары продажи всегда падают.
bulgarian: Sales always go down during a heat wave.

english: I'm lucky Holt and Celine are willing to help with the store, great for all of our overheads!
french: J'ai beaucoup de chances quand Holt et Céline m'aident au magasin, ça réduit nos frais !
russian: Повезло, что Хольт и Селин помогают с магазином: это всем нам на пользу!
bulgarian: I'm lucky Holt and Celine are willing to help with the store, great for all of our overheads!

english: Holt's not so good with spicy food...
french: Holt n'apprécie pas beaucoup la nourriture épicée...
russian: Хольт не очень переносит острую еду...
bulgarian: Holt's not so good with spicy food...

english: Hope I'll see you at the General Store today, [Ari].
french: J'espère que tu passeras au magasin général aujourd'hui, [Ari].
russian: Надеюсь, заглянешь сегодня в лавку, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hope I'll see you at the General Store today, [Ari].

english: No one does dinner like the Sleeping Dragon!
french: Les dîners servis au Dragon qui dort sont délicieux !
russian: Никто не готовит так, как «Спящий дракон»!
bulgarian: No one does dinner like the Sleeping Dragon!

english: Hmm, the balances don't match... I wonder if Holt's having himself a snack from the shop's inventory again...
french: Mmm, j'ai des écarts entre ce que j'achète et ce que je vends... Je me demande si Holt n'aurait pas recommencé à se servir dans la réserve...
russian: Хм, учёт не сходится... интересно, это Хольт снова таскает вкусненькое из магазина?
bulgarian: Hmm, the balances don't match... I wonder if Holt's having himself a snack from the shop's inventory again...

english: You can leave your tesserae by the till! And if you need help with something, just flag one of us down.
french: Laisse tes tesserae à côté de la caisse ! Et si tu as besoin d'un renseignement, fais-nous signe.
russian: Можешь оставить тессеры у кассы! А если нужна помощь — просто позови кого-нибудь из нас.
bulgarian: You can leave your tesserae by the till! And if you need help with something, just flag one of us down.

english: The General Store is part of the lifeblood of Mistria. That's what gets me up in the morning.
french: Le magasin général est un pilier de notre ville. C'est ce qui me motive pour me lever le matin.
russian: Универмаг — часть сердца Мистрии. Именно эта мысль поднимает меня по утрам.
bulgarian: The General Store is part of the lifeblood of Mistria. That's what gets me up in the morning.

english: If these three ever want to start a band, I'd be first in line to be their manager!
french: Si ces trois-là décident de former un groupe, je serai la première à leur proposer mes services en tant qu'agent !
russian: Если эти трое решат собрать группу, я первая стану их менеджером!
bulgarian: If these three ever want to start a band, I'd be first in line to be their manager!

english: A good merchant looks at the world as a series of opportunities. That's good advice for a farmer too, [Ari]!
french: Un bon marchand voit le monde comme une série d'opportunités. Cela vaut aussi pour l'agriculture, [Ari] !
russian: Хороший торговец смотрит на мир как на череду возможностей. Земледельцу это тоже пригодится, [Ari]!
bulgarian: A good merchant looks at the world as a series of opportunities. That's good advice for a farmer too, [Ari]!

english: It's my day to mind the shop, [Ari]! Thanks for coming by, it's always nice to see a friendly face.
french: C'est à mon tour de tenir la boutique aujourd'hui, [Ari] ! Merci de ta visite, c'est toujours un plaisir de voir un visage souriant.
russian:
Сегодня моя очередь сидеть в магазине, [Ari]! Спасибо, что

заглянули

заглянулазаглянулзаглянуло. Всегда приятно видеть знакомое лицо.
bulgarian: It's my day to mind the shop, [Ari]! Thanks for coming by, it's always nice to see a friendly face.

english: Morning, [Ari]! Hope you're keeping busy on this fine day.
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! J'imagine que tu n'arrêtes pas par une si belle journée.
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari]! Надеюсь, дела у тебя идут хорошо в такой прекрасный день.
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Hope you're keeping busy on this fine day.

english: Josephine's right! A morning bath is just the thing!
french: Joséphine a tout à fait raison ! Rien de tel qu'un bain de bon matin pour avoir de l'entrain !
russian: Джозефина права! Утренняя ванна — то, что нужно!
bulgarian: Josephine's right! A morning bath is just the thing!

english: Some morning shopping for you, [Ari]?
french: Tu es bien matinal<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they>, [Ari].
russian: Утренние покупки, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Some morning shopping for you, [Ari]?

english: Actually, Celine taught me how to make a salad. Hm.
french: En réalité, c'est Céline qui m'a appris comment faire. Hum.
russian: Хотя, на самом деле, это Селин меня научила. Хм.
bulgarian: Actually, Celine taught me how to make a salad. Hm.

english: I'm not quite the cook that Holt is, but I can make a fresh salad at least!
french: Je ne cuisine pas aussi bien que Holt, mais je sais au moins préparer une petite salade !
russian: Я не такой кулинар, как Хольт, но хоть свежий салат могу сделать!
bulgarian: I'm not quite the cook that Holt is, but I can make a fresh salad at least!

english: The numbers are looking good, Holt. It's an uptick from last month.
french: Par rapport au mois dernier, les chiffres sont bien meilleurs, Holt.
russian: Цифры радуют, Хольт. Рост по сравнению с прошлым месяцем.
bulgarian: The numbers are looking good, Holt. It's an uptick from last month.

english: I owe Josie some gossip... she always wants the latest on the Saturday Market.
french: J'ai quelques potins à raconter à Jo... Elle veut toujours tout savoir, quand vient le marché du samedi.
russian: Я задолжала Джози немного сплетен... она всегда хочет знать, что новенького на Субботнем базаре.
bulgarian: I owe Josie some gossip... she always wants the latest on the Saturday Market.

english: I hope Dell hasn't requisitioned it for the Dragonguard... again...
french: J'espère que Dell ne l'a pas encore « réquisitionné » pour la Garde des dragons...
russian: Надеюсь, Делл не забрала его для нужд Драконьей стражи... опять...
bulgarian: I hope Dell hasn't requisitioned it for the Dragonguard... again...

english: Now where did I put my pencil?
french: Où ai-je bien pu laisser traîner mon crayon ?
russian: Так... куда я положила карандаш?
bulgarian: Now where did I put my pencil?

english: The day after a Saturday Market always feels a bit slow by comparison.
french: Le dimanche après le marché, c'est toujours un peu calme.
russian: День после Субботнего базара всегда ощущается немного медленным.
bulgarian: The day after a Saturday Market always feels a bit slow by comparison.

english: The house looks extra cozy on rainy days...
french: Les jours de pluie, la maison paraît encore plus accueillante...
russian: В дождь дом кажется особенно уютным...
bulgarian: The house looks extra cozy on rainy days...

english: Unless I'm chasing Dell out of puddles.
french: À moins que je coure après Dell pour qu'elle ne saute pas dans les flaques.
russian: Если, конечно, не гоняю Делл из луж.
bulgarian: Unless I'm chasing Dell out of puddles.

english: Rain usually means it's slow at the General Store, so I take the day to run some errands.
french: Quand il pleut, c'est plutôt calme au magasin. J'en profite pour rattraper ce que je n'ai pas eu le temps de faire.
russian: В дождь в магазине обычно тихо, так что я занимаюсь делами по городу.
bulgarian: Rain usually means it's slow at the General Store, so I take the day to run some errands.

english: Everything's looking good for the Market tomorrow! Now I can enjoy Inn night without any worries.
french: Je crois que tout est prêt pour le marché de demain ! Je vais pouvoir me détendre à l'auberge, ce soir.
russian: Всё готово к завтрашнему базару! Можно спокойно наслаждаться вечером в трактире.
bulgarian: Everything's looking good for the Market tomorrow! Now I can enjoy Inn night without any worries.

english: Welcome, [Ari]! Have a look around and let me know if you have any questions.
french: Bienvenue, [Ari] ! Jette un œil et n'hésite pas si tu as la moindre question.
russian: Добро пожаловать, [Ari]! Оглянись как следует и дай знать, если будут вопросы.
bulgarian: Welcome, [Ari]! Have a look around and let me know if you have any questions.

english: Are you looking for Celine? She took a different shift this week.
french: Tu cherches Céline ? Elle n'a pas les mêmes horaires, cette semaine.
russian: Ищешь Селин? У неё на этой неделе другой график.
bulgarian: Are you looking for Celine? She took a different shift this week.

english: Take your time, I'm happy to help when you're ready.
french: Prends ton temps et dis-moi si je peux t'aider.
russian:
Не торопись, я помогу, когда будешь

готовы

готоваготовготово.
bulgarian: Take your time, I'm happy to help when you're ready.

english: We just restocked, [Ari]! Have a good look around.
french: Nous venons de nous réapprovisionner, [Ari] ! Vois si quelque chose te plaît.
russian: Мы только что пополнили запасы, [Ari]! Осмотрись хорошенько.
bulgarian: We just restocked, [Ari]! Have a good look around.

english: I just had an idea for the Saturday Market, but it'll have to wait till after my shift is over.
french: Je viens d'avoir une idée pour le marché, mais je vais devoir attendre la relève.
russian: Мне только что пришла идея для Субботнего базара, но придётся подождать до конца смены.
bulgarian: I just had an idea for the Saturday Market, but it'll have to wait till after my shift is over.

english: An organized shelf is a happy shelf!
french: Un rayon bien rangé attire les regards !
russian: Упорядоченная полка — счастливая полка!
bulgarian: An organized shelf is a happy shelf!

english: Balor's always bringing us produce you shipped! Thanks for your hard work, [Ari].
french: Balor n'arrête pas de nous apporter les produits que tu lui confies ! Merci de travailler si dur, [Ari].
russian: Балор всё время приносит нам урожай, который ты отправляешь! Спасибо за твою работу, [Ari].
bulgarian: Balor's always bringing us produce you shipped! Thanks for your hard work, [Ari].

english: "Omelet that slide."
french: « Même pas un petit bout de pain, ma mie ? »
russian: «Ну и оладно!»
bulgarian: "Omelet that slide."

english: Hahaha!
french: Ha ha ha !
russian: Ха-ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Hahaha!

english: Hahaha, [Ari]... my husband, I can't take it. I told him I was going to skip breakfast, and you know what he said?
french: Ha ha ha, [Ari]... Quel blagueur, mon mari ! Je lui ai dit que je comptais sauter le petit-déjeuner, et tu sais ce qu'il m'a répondu ?
russian: Ха-ха-ха, [Ari]... мой муж, я не могу с него. Я сказала, что пропущу завтрак, а он, знаешь, что ответил?
bulgarian: Hahaha, [Ari]... my husband, I can't take it. I told him I was going to skip breakfast, and you know what he said?

english: I think you could drive the economy of Mistria singlehandedly, [Ari]. I've never seen one person go through so much tesserae.
french: J'ai l'impression qu'à toi seul<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they>, tu pourrais faire tourner tout Mistria. Je n'ai jamais vu personne brasser autant de tesserae.
russian: Думаю, ты можешь в одиночку разогнать экономику Мистрии, [Ari]. Никогда не видела, чтобы один человек так активно тратил тессеры.
bulgarian: I think you could drive the economy of Mistria singlehandedly, [Ari]. I've never seen one person go through so much tesserae.

english: Oh, I do so love the look of a properly restocked shelf.
french: Oh, j'aime quand une étagère est bien remplie.
russian: О, как же я люблю вид аккуратно укомплектованной полки.
bulgarian: Oh, I do so love the look of a properly restocked shelf.

english: I'm still recovering from yesterday's Market Day, but I'm already planning for next week!
french: Je me remets encore du marché d'hier, mais je fais déjà des préparatifs pour la semaine prochaine !
russian: Я ещё не оправилась после вчерашнего базарного дня, а уже строю планы на следующий!
bulgarian: I'm still recovering from yesterday's Market Day, but I'm already planning for next week!

english: Sales go up when the sun's out.
french: Quand il fait beau, les ventes s'envolent.
russian: Когда светит солнце, продажи растут.
bulgarian: Sales go up when the sun's out.

english: A tidy store really puts my mind at ease.
french: Je ne me sens bien que quand je vois le magasin bien rangé.
russian: Чистый магазин сразу наводит порядок в голове.
bulgarian: A tidy store really puts my mind at ease.

english: Thanks for your patronage, [Ari]. Let me know if you need anything.
french: Merci de ta fidélité, [Ari]. Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, n'hésite pas.
russian: Спасибо за покупку, [Ari]. Дай знать, если что-нибудь понадобится.
bulgarian: Thanks for your patronage, [Ari]. Let me know if you need anything.

english: That's my girl!
french: Quelle chance j'ai d'avoir une fille comme elle !
russian: Вот это моя девочка!
bulgarian: That's my girl!

english: Oh, don't mind me, just tidying up while Celine is out. Can you believe she dusts the plants?
french: Oh, ne fais pas attention à moi. Je fais un brin de ménage pendant que Céline n'est pas là. Elle dépoussière même les plantes, tu le crois ça ?
russian: Не обращай внимания, я тут просто убираюсь, пока Селин нет. Представляешь, она пыль даже с растений вытирает!
bulgarian: Oh, don't mind me, just tidying up while Celine is out. Can you believe she dusts the plants?

english: Celine's very busy this week, so I thought I'd drop by and tidy up for her.
french: Céline a fort à faire cette semaine. Je me suis dit que j'allais passer faire un peu de rangement.
russian: У Селин на этой неделе много дел, так что я решила заглянуть и прибраться за неё.
bulgarian: Celine's very busy this week, so I thought I'd drop by and tidy up for her.

english: Maybe I'll just tidy up a little bit.
french: Je vais peut-être faire un peu de ménage.
russian: Наверное, просто немного приберусь.
bulgarian: Maybe I'll just tidy up a little bit.

english: Oh hey, [Ari]! I thought I'd check on Celine, but she's not here.
french: Tiens, bonjour [Ari] ! Je venais voir Céline, mais elle n'est pas là.
russian: О, привет, [Ari]! Я хотела навестить Селин, но её нет.
bulgarian: Oh hey, [Ari]! I thought I'd check on Celine, but she's not here.

english: I thought I'd come by and tidy up, but she keeps the place pretty clean! That's my girl.
french: Je pensais faire un petit peu de ménage, mais c'est déjà impeccable. Ma fille est merveilleuse !
russian: Я пришла немного прибраться, но у неё и так всё чисто! Вот это моя девочка.
bulgarian: I thought I'd come by and tidy up, but she keeps the place pretty clean! That's my girl.

english: Oh, were you looking for Celine? She's out.
french: Oh, tu viens voir Céline ? Elle n'est pas là.
russian: Ты Селин ищешь? Её нет.
bulgarian: Oh, were you looking for Celine? She's out.

english: Celine keeps her place pretty clean! I don't know if I need to be tidying up for her anymore.
french: Céline aime que sa maison soit propre ! Je ne sais pas si ça vaut encore la peine que je passe lui faire du ménage.
russian: Селин хорошо убирается! Похоже, мне уже и не нужно ей помогать.
bulgarian: Celine keeps her place pretty clean! I don't know if I need to be tidying up for her anymore.

english: That Balor is tight-lipped about his suppliers, but I'll crack him yet.
french: Ce Balor... Il ne veut pas dire où il se fournit, mais j'arriverai à le faire parler.
russian: Балор не хочет раскрывать, откуда он берёт товары, но я его рано или поздно раскручу.
bulgarian: That Balor is tight-lipped about his suppliers, but I'll crack him yet.

english: I can ring you up whenever you're ready.
french: Je suis prête à t'encaisser dès que tu auras terminé.
russian:

english: Hey, thanks!

russian: О-о, что это? Гранит? Круто. Блестящие вкрапления — это кристаллы! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Ooh, what's this? Granite? Sweet. You can tell by the shiny bits, those are crystal! Thanks, [Ari]!

russian: Камень тёмный... мелкозернистый... мало кремния... это базальт! Спасибо, [Ari], ты отлично пополняешь мою коллекцию!
bulgarian: This stone is pretty dark... fine grain... low in silica... it's basalt! Thanks [Ari], you're really helping me grow my rock collection.

russian: Так... гладкий на ощупь... чередуются светлые и тёмные полосы... довольно твёрдый... это сланец! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Let's see... smooth to the touch... alternating bands of light and dark... pretty hard... this is schist! Thanks, [Ari]!

english: Celine uses them for composting, which is kind of poetic if you think about it.
french: Céline s'en sert pour son compost, ce qui a un côté assez poétique.
russian: Селин использует их для компоста, и это как-то даже поэтично, если подумать.
bulgarian: Celine uses them for composting, which is kind of poetic if you think about it.

english: We always end up with a lot of scraps after a day of cooking.
french: Il y a toujours beaucoup de déchets, après une journée passée à cuisiner.
russian: После дня готовки остаётся куча отходов.
bulgarian: We always end up with a lot of scraps after a day of cooking.

english: It's a sleepy Sunday! Come in and relax with me before the new week starts!
french: C'est un dimanche relax ! Viens te détendre avec moi avant que la semaine ne recommence !
russian: Сегодня сонное воскресенье! Заходи, отдохни со мной, пока не началась новая неделя!
bulgarian: It's a sleepy Sunday! Come in and relax with me before the new week starts!

english: Hi [Ari]! Go on and make yourself at home.
french: Salut [Ari] ! Mets-toi à l'aise et fais comme chez toi.
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Располагайся, как дома.
bulgarian: Hi [Ari]! Go on and make yourself at home.

english: The kitchen is so cozy in the fall! I love it!
french: Je me sens si bien dans la cuisine, en automne ! J'adore !
russian: На кухне осенью так уютно! Я просто в восторге!
bulgarian: The kitchen is so cozy in the fall! I love it!

english: I used to hate doing inventory, but now I think of it as a gift for tomorrow's Reina.
french: Avant, je détestais faire l'inventaire. Maintenant, je vois ça comme un cadeau de la Reina de demain.
russian: Раньше я ненавидела вести учёт, а теперь думаю, что, если сделаю его сегодня, это будет подарок для завтрашней Рейны.
bulgarian: I used to hate doing inventory, but now I think of it as a gift for tomorrow's Reina.

english: Balor's been staying at the Inn for a good long while now, and I still don't know the first thing about him! Maybe YOU can get him out of that shell, [Ari].
french: Balor séjourne à l'auberge depuis un bon moment maintenant, et je ne sais toujours rien de lui ! Tu arriveras peut-être à lui tirer les vers du nez, [Ari].
russian: Балор уже долго живёт в трактире, а я до сих пор о нём ничего не знаю! Может, ТЫ его разговоришь, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Balor's been staying at the Inn for a good long while now, and I still don't know the first thing about him! Maybe YOU can get him out of that shell, [Ari].

english: Maybe YOU can get him out of that shell, [Ari].
french: Tu arriveras peut-être à lui tirer les vers du nez, [Ari].
russian: Может, у ТЕБЯ получится пробиться сквозь его броню, [Ari].
bulgarian: Maybe YOU can get him out of that shell, [Ari].

english: Balor likes to keep to himself. I still don't know the first thing about him!
french: Balor séjourne à l'auberge depuis un bon moment maintenant, et je ne sais toujours rien de lui ! Tu arriveras peut-être à lui tirer les vers du nez, [Ari].
russian: Балор уже довольно давно живёт в нашем трактире, а я до сих пор о нём ничего не знаю! Может, у ТЕБЯ получится пробиться сквозь его броню, [Ari].
bulgarian: Balor likes to keep to himself. I still don't know the first thing about him!

english: Landen and Ryis are a funny pair... one won't stop talking and the other won't start! Sometimes it's hard to believe they're related!
french: Landen et Ryis forment une drôle d'équipe... L'un n'arrête pas de parler et l'autre est muet comme une carpe ! Parfois, je me demande s'ils sont vraiment parents !
russian: Ланден и Риз — забавная парочка... один не замолкает, другой держит рот на замке! И ведь родственники!
bulgarian: Landen and Ryis are a funny pair... one won't stop talking and the other won't start! Sometimes it's hard to believe they're related!

english: It reminds me of how everyone looked after me, Adeline and Celine when we were their age!
french: Ça me rappelle la façon dont tout le monde s'occupait d'Adeline, Céline et moi au même âge !
russian: Напоминает, как когда-то все заботились о нас с Аделиной и Селин!
bulgarian: It reminds me of how everyone looked after me, Adeline and Celine when we were their age!

english: It's so sweet how the whole town looks after Maple, Luc and Dell.
french: C'est vraiment adorable de la part des habitants de la ville de s'occuper si bien de Maple, Luc et Dell.
russian: Так мило, что весь город заботится о Мэйпл, Люке и Делл.
bulgarian: It's so sweet how the whole town looks after Maple, Luc and Dell.

english: Between you and me, [Ari], I've always wondered what's going on with Errol, Landen and Terithia... it looks like a little bit of a love triangle to me! You better tell me any juicy gossip, ok?
french: [Ari], je me suis toujours demandé ce qu'il y avait entre Errol, Landen et Terithia. Ils ne seraient pas tous les deux amoureux d'elle ?! Si tu as des infos à ce sujet, viens me voir !
russian: Скажу по секрету, [Ari]: по-моему, между Эрролом, Ланденом и Теризией что-то есть... Неужто любовный треугольник? Если узнаешь слухи, расскажи, ладно?
bulgarian: Between you and me, [Ari], I've always wondered what's going on with Errol, Landen and Terithia... it looks like a little bit of a love triangle to me! You better tell me any juicy gossip, ok?

english: Me too, honestly.
french: Et moi aussi, à vrai dire.
russian: Честно? Я тоже.
bulgarian: Me too, honestly.

english: Maple and Luc are crazy for =Cheese= lately.
french: Ces derniers temps, Maple et Luc ne jurent que par le =fromage=.
russian: Мэйпл и Люк в последнее время без ума от =сыра=.
bulgarian: Maple and Luc are crazy for =Cheese= lately.

english: Luc is always showing me his bug friends! At first it was hard because I thought bugs were icky, but now I think they're kinda cute...
french: Luc n'arrête pas de me montrer ses insectes ! Au début, j'avais du mal parce que je les trouvais plutôt répugnants, mais au final, ils sont assez mignons...
russian: Люк постоянно показывает мне своих друзей-жуков! Сначала было тяжело: я ведь считала насекомых фу-фу, — а теперь они вроде даже милые...
bulgarian: Luc is always showing me his bug friends! At first it was hard because I thought bugs were icky, but now I think they're kinda cute...

english: I'm having such a nice day off! Look at all those pretty fall colors!
french: Ma journée de repos est très agréable ! Ces tonalités automnales sont si jolies !
russian: Сегодня у меня такой чудесный выходной! Посмотри на все эти красивые осенние краски!
bulgarian: I'm having such a nice day off! Look at all those pretty fall colors!

english: Maybe I'll pick some for Luc and Maple!
french: Je vais peut-être en cueillir pour Maple et Luc, tout à l'heure.
russian: Может, соберу немного для Люка и Мэйпл!
bulgarian: Maybe I'll pick some for Luc and Maple!

english: The $Violas$ are so pretty! Look, [Ari]!
french: Et ces $violettes$ sont magnifiques ! Regarde, [Ari] !
russian: Какие красивые $фиалки$! Смотри, [Ari]!
bulgarian: The $Violas$ are so pretty! Look, [Ari]!

english: That's made Luc really happy! Celine is his hero!
french: Luc est très heureux ! Céline est son héroïne !
russian: Это так радует Люка! Селин — его героиня!
bulgarian: That's made Luc really happy! Celine is his hero!

english: Ever since Celine started doing upkeep on the manor garden, it seems like the insects that rely on the garden have also been thriving.
french: Depuis que Céline s'occupe du jardin du manoir, les insectes qui y nichent semblent se porter encore mieux.
russian: С тех пор, как Селин стала ухаживать за садом особняка, насекомым, которые там обитают, тоже хорошо стало житься!
bulgarian: Ever since Celine started doing upkeep on the manor garden, it seems like the insects that rely on the garden have also been thriving.

english: Those are $Violas$, and those are $Celosia$! Aren't they pretty?
french: Ça, c'est des $violettes$, et ça, des $célosies$ ! Elles sont belles, non ?
russian: Там — $фиалки$, а вон там — $целозии$! Красивые, правда?
bulgarian: Those are $Violas$, and those are $Celosia$! Aren't they pretty?

english: Celine taught me the names of the flowers that she grows on the Manor grounds in fall!
french: Céline m'a appris le nom des fleurs qu'elle fait pousser dans les jardins du manoir à l'automne.
russian: Селин рассказала мне, как называются цветы, которые она выращивает у особняка осенью.
bulgarian: Celine taught me the names of the flowers that she grows on the Manor grounds in fall!

english: Maple and Luc were so cute this morning! I'm such a lucky big sister.
french: Maple et Luc étaient adorables, ce matin ! J'ai beaucoup de chance d'être leur grande sœur.
russian: Мэйпл и Люк сегодня утром были такие милые! Я такая счастливая старшая сестра.
bulgarian: Maple and Luc were so cute this morning! I'm such a lucky big sister.

english: I tried to let Maple down easy that she can't be a princess when she grows up, but she dragged out the rules and regulations of Mistria, and I guess there are a lot of loopholes?
french: J'ai tenté d'expliquer à Maple qu'elle ne pourrait pas devenir princesse une fois adulte, mais elle a sorti la constitution de Mistria et effectivement, il y a pas mal de failles.
russian: Я пыталась мягко объяснить Мэйпл, что она не сможет стать принцессой, когда вырастет, но она достала правила Мистрии — и, кажется, там полно лазеек.
bulgarian: I tried to let Maple down easy that she can't be a princess when she grows up, but she dragged out the rules and regulations of Mistria, and I guess there are a lot of loopholes?

english: Honestly it's Eiland and Adeline's problem at this point.
french: À dire vrai, c'est à Adeline et Eiland de gérer désormais.
russian: Думаю, теперь это проблема Эйланда и Аделины.
bulgarian: Honestly it's Eiland and Adeline's problem at this point.

english: Prep goes so much faster since I commissioned a set from him.
french: Je passe bien moins de temps à parer la viande ou émincer les légumes depuis que je lui en ai acheté de nouveaux.
russian: С ними подготовка идёт куда быстрее!
bulgarian: Prep goes so much faster since I commissioned a set from him.

english: March is such a crank, but his knives are amazing.
french: March est un drôle d'hurluberlu, mais ses couteaux sont de très bonne qualité.
russian: Март такой ворчун, но его ножи — потрясающие.
bulgarian: March is such a crank, but his knives are amazing.

english: I've got some killer ideas for next week's menu. Keep an eye out!
french: J'ai des idées fantastiques pour le menu de la semaine prochaine. J'espère que tu y goûteras !
russian: У меня классные идеи для меню на следующую неделю. Следи за обновлениями!
bulgarian: I've got some killer ideas for next week's menu. Keep an eye out!

english: I'm usually in the kitchen cooking, so working the till is a nice change of pace.
french: En général, je suis aux fourneaux, alors ça me change un peu de m'occuper de la caisse.
russian: Я обычно на кухне, но работать за кассой — приятная смена обстановки.
bulgarian: I'm usually in the kitchen cooking, so working the till is a nice change of pace.

english: Ma and I have got this kitchen humming! There's already some folks trickling in... nothing like a good stew after coming in from the rain.
french: Maman et moi sommes bien affairées derrière les fourneaux ! Il y a déjà du monde qui arrive... Rien ne vaut une bonne assiette de ragoût quand il pleut.
russian: Мы с мамой так наладили кухню, что она просто поёт! Уже начинают приходить гости... ничего нет лучше, чем горячее рагу после дождя.
bulgarian: Ma and I have got this kitchen humming! There's already some folks trickling in... nothing like a good stew after coming in from the rain.

english: Today's menu at the Sleeping Dragon is going to be curry, stews... maybe some fresh bread? Everything you could want to get cozy after a walk in the rain.
french: Aujourd'hui, au Dragon qui dort, nous proposons du curry et du ragoût... Peut-être un peu de pain frais aussi ? Tout ce qu'il faut après avoir marché sous la pluie.
russian: Сегодня в меню «Спящего дракона» карри, рагу... может, свежий хлеб? Всё, чтобы согреться после прогулки под дождём.
bulgarian: Today's menu at the Sleeping Dragon is going to be curry, stews... maybe some fresh bread? Everything you could want to get cozy after a walk in the rain.

english: A lot of folks gather at the Inn on rainy days, so I'm stocking up... gotta be sure there's enough to feed every guest and then some!
french: Beaucoup de gens viennent à l'auberge, les jours de pluie, alors je fais des provisions... Il faut prévoir suffisamment pour tous les clients, et même un peu plus !
russian: В дождь в трактире собирается много народу, так что я делаю запасы... нужно быть уверенной, что еды хватит всем — и ещё останется!
bulgarian: A lot of folks gather at the Inn on rainy days, so I'm stocking up... gotta be sure there's enough to feed every guest and then some!

english: And we always keep the soup pot going for people coming out of the rain!
french: Et il y a toujours de la soupe chaude pour les gens qui arrivent détrempés !
russian: И у нас всегда стоит суп для тех, кто приходит с улицы!
bulgarian: And we always keep the soup pot going for people coming out of the rain!

english: Rainy days are so busy at the Inn! But I always look forward to whoever might drop by.
french: Il y a toujours beaucoup de monde à l'auberge quand il pleut, mais on ne sait jamais exactement qui passera.
russian: Дождливые дни в трактире всегда такие загруженные! Но я люблю каждого, кто заходит ко мне.
bulgarian: Rainy days are so busy at the Inn! But I always look forward to whoever might drop by.

english: A rainy day like this would be perfect for snuggling up with a good book...
french: Une journée pluvieuse comme aujourd'hui serait parfaite pour se blottir au chaud avec un bon bouquin...
russian: В такой дождливый день самое то — устроиться поуютнее с хорошей книгой...
bulgarian: A rainy day like this would be perfect for snuggling up with a good book...

english: The sound of the rain is so cozy... it makes me want to relax and read a book.
french: Le bruit de la pluie est tellement réconfortant... Ça me donne envie de me détendre en lisant un livre.
russian: Шум дождя такой уютный... так и хочется расслабиться и почитать книгу.
bulgarian: The sound of the rain is so cozy... it makes me want to relax and read a book.

english: Nothing better than some soup on a rainy day.
french: Rien ne vaut un bon potage un jour de pluie.
russian: Нет ничего лучше супа в дождливый день.
bulgarian: Nothing better than some soup on a rainy day.

english: I can't wait to unwind with a good book later...
french: J'ai hâte de me relaxer avec un bon livre, tout à l'heure...
russian: Скорее бы уже вечером отдохнуть с хорошей книгой...
bulgarian: I can't wait to unwind with a good book later...

english: There's so much to do today!
french: Il y a tellement à faire, aujourd'hui !
russian: Сегодня столько дел!
bulgarian: There's so much to do today!

english: Now where were we... Ah yes. The duchy's complex politics meant there was no clear successor-
french: Alors, on en était où...? Ah oui. La situation politique inextricable du duché empêcha la désignation formelle d'un successeur...
russian: Так, на чём мы остановились... Ах да. Сложная политика герцогства означала, что явного наследника не было...
bulgarian: Now where were we... Ah yes. The duchy's complex politics meant there was no clear successor-

english: Watch me!
french: Je te le garantis !
russian: Вот увидишь!
bulgarian: Watch me!

english: Phew! I'm a little behind schedule, but I'll be ready by the time people start rolling in!
french: Pfiou ! J'ai pris un peu en retard, mais je serai fin prête pour les premiers clients.
russian: Фух! Немного отстаю от графика, но к приходу людей я успею!
bulgarian: Phew! I'm a little behind schedule, but I'll be ready by the time people start rolling in!

english: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn, [Ari]! Make yourself at home!
french: Bienvenue à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort, [Ari] ! Mets-toi à l'aise.
russian: Добро пожаловать в трактир «Спящий дракон», [Ari]! Чувствуй себя как дома!
bulgarian: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn, [Ari]! Make yourself at home!

english: It's always nice when you come around, [Ari]. Now, what can I get for you?
french: C'est toujours un plaisir de te voir, [Ari] ! Dis-moi, qu'est-ce qui te ferait plaisir ?
russian: Всегда приятно, когда ты заглядываешь, [Ari]. Ну, что приготовить для тебя?
bulgarian: It's always nice when you come around, [Ari]. Now, what can I get for you?

english: Take a peek at the menu and let me know if I can cook something up for you, [Ari]!
french: Jette un œil au menu et dis-moi ce que tu veux que je te prépare, [Ari] !
russian: Загляни в меню и скажи, чего тебе хочется, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Take a peek at the menu and let me know if I can cook something up for you, [Ari]!

english: Sometimes I even run into Celine! Or you!
french: Et parfois je tombe sur Céline ! Ou sur toi !
russian: Иногда даже встречаю Селин! Или тебя!
bulgarian: Sometimes I even run into Celine! Or you!

english: It's nice that I can pop over here if we're missing anything in the kitchen.
french: Si jamais il nous manque quelque chose en cuisine, je peux toujours faire un saut ici. C'est très pratique !
russian: Хорошо, что я могу забежать сюда, если чего-то не хватает на кухне.
bulgarian: It's nice that I can pop over here if we're missing anything in the kitchen.

english: I love running into Elsie when I'm out here. She has the best stories!
french: J'adore croiser Elsie quand je me balade. Elle a toujours des histoires très intéressantes !
russian: Обожаю натыкаться на Элси, когда выхожу сюда. У неё лучшие истории!
bulgarian: I love running into Elsie when I'm out here. She has the best stories!

english: And she just... disappeared the jar!
french: Elle a simplement... fait disparaître le bocal !
russian: И она её просто... развоплотила!
bulgarian: And she just... disappeared the jar!

english: She didn't even offer to help clean up! There were pickles everywhere!
french: Elle n'a même pas proposé de m'aider à nettoyer. Il y avait des cornichons partout !
russian: И даже не предложила за собой убрать! А там повсюду огурцы валялись!
bulgarian: She didn't even offer to help clean up! There were pickles everywhere!

english: I asked Seridia to help me open a pickle jar the other day...
french: J'ai demandé à Seridia de m'aider à ouvrir un bocal de cornichons, l'autre jour...
russian: Недавно я попросила Серидию помочь мне открыть банку солёных огурцов...
bulgarian: I asked Seridia to help me open a pickle jar the other day...

english: I left a =Crystal Berry Pie= on the counter to cool, and it suddenly up and vanished, like magic!
french: J'avais laissé une =tarte aux baies de cristal= à refroidir sur le comptoir, et elle s'est volatilisée d'un coup, comme par magie !
russian: Я поставила =пирог из кристальных ягод= остывать на стойку, а он вдруг взял и исчез! Какая-то магия!
bulgarian: I left a =Crystal Berry Pie= on the counter to cool, and it suddenly up and vanished, like magic!

english: I wonder where it flew off to...
french: Je me demande où elle s'est envolée...
russian: Интересно, и куда же он улетел...
bulgarian: I wonder where it flew off to...

english: So weird...
french: C'est bizarre...
russian: Как странно...
bulgarian: So weird...

english: I nibbled so much while working in the kitchen, I ended up skipping dinner.
french: J'ai tellement grignoté en cuisinant que j'ai fini par me passer de dîner.
russian: Я столько всего понадкусывала на кухне, что в итоге пропустила ужин.
bulgarian: I nibbled so much while working in the kitchen, I ended up skipping dinner.

english: That's wrong, but it's also really cute...
french: Il se trompe, mais je la trouve mignonne, cette erreur...
russian: Это неправильно, но и очень мило...
bulgarian: That's wrong, but it's also really cute...

english: Olric's always calling it "The Sleepy Dragon Inn".
french: Olric appelle toujours cet endroit « l'auberge du Dragon qui sort ».
russian: Ольрик постоянно называет нас «Трактир "Сонный драгун"».
bulgarian: Olric's always calling it "The Sleepy Dragon Inn".

english: What a nice, slow day. I'm always a little sleepier after Market Day.
french: C'est une journée calme et reposante. Je me sens toujours un peu fatiguée, les lendemains de marché.
russian: Какой приятный спокойный день. После базарного дня я всегда немного сонная.
bulgarian: What a nice, slow day. I'm always a little sleepier after Market Day.

english: You hungry, [Ari]? The soup came out pretty good today. Don't be shy now, grab a bowl!
french: Tu as un petit creux, [Ari] ? La soupe est vraiment bonne, aujourd'hui. Va donc te servir un bol !
russian:
Голодны

ГолоднаГолоденГолодное, [Ari]? Суп сегодня получился отличный. Не стесняйся, бери миску!
bulgarian: You hungry, [Ari]? The soup came out pretty good today. Don't be shy now, grab a bowl!

english: The soup came out nice today, in my humble opinion.
french: En toute modestie, je trouve que la soupe est bonne aujourd'hui.
russian: По моему скромному мнению, суп сегодня удался.
bulgarian: The soup came out nice today, in my humble opinion.

english: Hi, [Ari]! Take a seat and have yourself something tasty!
french: Coucou, [Ari] ! Assieds-toi et commande ce qui te tente !
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Садись, перекуси чем-нибудь вкусненьким!
bulgarian: Hi, [Ari]! Take a seat and have yourself something tasty!

english: Don't be all shy about it!
french: Fais comme chez toi !
russian: Не стесняйся!
bulgarian: Don't be all shy about it!

english: There's the free soup, and our menu at the front, but if you ever want to make a meal yourself you're more than welcome to use our kitchen!
french: On te propose notre soupe gratuite ou le menu du jour est affiché au niveau de la caisse. Mais si tu veux te cuisiner quelque chose, aucun problème !
russian:
Есть бесплатный суп и меню у входа, но если хочешь приготовить что-то

сами

самасамсамо — кухня твоя!
bulgarian: There's the free soup, and our menu at the front, but if you ever want to make a meal yourself you're more than welcome to use our kitchen!

english: Folks really went through the soup today! I'll have to make sure I remember this recipe... I was just winging it!
french: Tout le monde s'est jeté sur la soupe, aujourd'hui ! Il faudra que je me rappelle bien de la recette... J'ai improvisé !

bulgarian: I guess dreams do come true, huh?

english: My parents were recently reminiscing about the day they met.
french: Mes parents se remémoraient récemment le jour où ils se sont rencontrés.
russian: Недавно мои родители вспоминали, как они познакомились.
bulgarian: My parents were recently reminiscing about the day they met.

english: Oh, haha! Yeah.
french: Oh, ha ha ! Oui.
russian: Ой, ха-ха! Да.
bulgarian: Oh, haha! Yeah.

english: The book I'm reading had a really unexpected twist. It was so sad, I can't stop thinking about it!
french: Il y a eu un rebondissement vraiment inattendu dans le livre que je lisais. C'était tellement triste que je n'arrête pas d'y repenser !
russian: Я читаю одну книгу, и там всё неожиданно стало так грустно. Не могу выкинуть из головы!
bulgarian: The book I'm reading had a really unexpected twist. It was so sad, I can't stop thinking about it!

english: I tend to get pretty absorbed into whatever I'm currently reading...
french: J'ai tendance à être totalement absorbée par ce que je suis en train de lire...
russian: Я часто сильно погружаюсь в книги...
bulgarian: I tend to get pretty absorbed into whatever I'm currently reading...

english: I definitely need to make time later and find out what happens next.
french: Il faut absolument que je trouve le temps tout à l'heure de savoir ce qui se passe ensuite.
russian: Надо обязательно выделить время и прочитать, что будет дальше.
bulgarian: I definitely need to make time later and find out what happens next.

english: I'll lend you the book after I'm done and we can talk about it, I'd love to hear what you think!
french: Je te prêterai le livre quand je l'aurai fini. Comme ça on pourra en discuter, j'aimerais beaucoup avoir ton avis !
russian: Когда дочитаю, одолжу тебе эту книгу. Потом обсудим, мне очень хочется услышать твоё мнение!
bulgarian: I'll lend you the book after I'm done and we can talk about it, I'd love to hear what you think!

english: Sigh...
french: Soupir...
russian: Вздох...
bulgarian: Sigh...

bulgarian: Is everything okay?

english: Something on your mind?

russian: О чём думаешь?
bulgarian: Something on your mind?

english: When I go to the Inn now, I'm always struck by how busy it is.
french: Quand je vais à l'auberge, maintenant, je suis toujours frappée par l'activité qui y règne.
russian: Теперь, когда я захожу в трактир, меня всегда удивляет, как много там народу.
bulgarian: When I go to the Inn now, I'm always struck by how busy it is.

english: People are always coming and going, there's always something going on at all times of day.
french: Les gens vont et viennent, il se passe toujours quelque chose de nouveau à n'importe quelle heure du jour.
russian: Люди приходят и уходят, круглые сутки внутри что-то происходит.
bulgarian: People are always coming and going, there's always something going on at all times of day.

english: Here on [farm_name] with you though... it's bustling in its own way, but...
french: Ici, à [farm_name], avec toi... Il y a aussi une forme d'animation, mais...
russian: А [farm_name], где мы с тобой живём... Здесь тоже по-своему оживлённо, но...
bulgarian: Here on [farm_name] with you though... it's bustling in its own way, but...

english: It's also really peaceful, you know? It feels like our own special place.
french: C'est aussi très paisible, tu vois ? Comme si c'était un lieu rien qu'à nous.
russian: Ещё тут очень спокойно. Ты понимаешь, о чём я? Как будто это наше укромное местечко.
bulgarian: It's also really peaceful, you know? It feels like our own special place.

english: It's nice.
french: C'est agréable.
russian: Тут хорошо.
bulgarian: It's nice.

english: It's interesting...
french: C'est intéressant...
russian: Интересно...
bulgarian: It's interesting...

english: I got so used to being the one that takes care of everyone else...
french: J'ai été tellement habituée à ce que ce soit moi qui prenne soin de tous les autres...
russian: Я привыкла, что это я обо всех забочусь...
bulgarian: I got so used to being the one that takes care of everyone else...

english: Customers, my younger siblings, even my parents to some degree. Is it because I'm the eldest sister? Or inheritor of the Inn? I'm not sure.
french: Les clients, mon frère et ma sœur plus jeunes, mes parents, un peu. Parce que je suis l'aînée ? Que j'hériterai de l'auberge ? Je ne sais pas trop.
russian: О клиентах, о брате с сестрой, иногда и о родителях. Это потому что я старшая сестра? Или потому что я наследница семейного дела? Не знаю.
bulgarian: Customers, my younger siblings, even my parents to some degree. Is it because I'm the eldest sister? Or inheritor of the Inn? I'm not sure.

english: But now... I truly feel like I get to experience being someone's top priority.
french: Mais à présent... J'ai vraiment l'impression de découvrir ce que c'est d'être la priorité de quelqu'un.
russian: А теперь... Я могу почувствовать, каково это — быть для кого-то самым важным человеком.
bulgarian: But now... I truly feel like I get to experience being someone's top priority.

english: At least, that's how you make me feel.
french: Du moins, c'est l'impression que tu me donnes.
russian: По крайней мере, рядом с тобой я чувствую себя именно так.
bulgarian: At least, that's how you make me feel.

english: I love you, [Ari]. Your care means the world to me.
french: Je t'aime, [Ari]. Ça signifie beaucoup, pour moi, que tu prennes soin de moi.
russian: Я люблю тебя, [Ari]. И очень ценю твою заботу.
bulgarian: I love you, [Ari]. Your care means the world to me.

english: You're always checking in on me, [Ari].
french: Tu viens toujours voir si je vais bien, [Ari].
russian: Ты всегда находишь время меня проведать, [Ari].
bulgarian: You're always checking in on me, [Ari].

english: You're looking extra good today, [Ari].
french: Tu resplendis, aujourd'hui, [Ari].
russian: Ты сегодня шикарно выглядишь, [Ari].
bulgarian: You're looking extra good today, [Ari].

english: Hehe! I'm a lucky lady...
french: Hi hi ! J'ai bien de la chance...
russian: Хи-хи! Повезло мне с тобой...
bulgarian: Hehe! I'm a lucky lady...

english: Not as lucky as me!
french: Pas autant que moi !
russian: А мне с тобой ещё больше!
bulgarian: Not as lucky as me!

english: Let's hope my lucky streak continues...
french: Espérons que je continue d'avoir autant de chance...
russian: А дальше будет только лучше...
bulgarian: Let's hope my lucky streak continues...

english: Oh, you!
french: Oh, toi alors !
russian: Ах, ты меня засмущаешь!
bulgarian: Oh, you!

french: Viens ici m'embrasser !
russian: Иди-ка сюда, дай поцелую!
bulgarian: Come here and give me a kiss!

english: Hmmm I guess you'll just have to wait and find out!
french: Hmm, je crois que tu vas devoir attendre pour le savoir !
russian: Хмм, ловлю тебя на слове!
bulgarian: Hmmm I guess you'll just have to wait and find out!

english: Come here and give me a kiss!
french: Viens ici m'embrasser !
russian: Иди-ка сюда, дай поцелую!
bulgarian: Come here and give me a kiss!

english: Oh!
french: Oh !
russian: Ой!
bulgarian: Oh!

english: So much has happened... It makes me excited about what's to come.
french: Il s'est passé tant de choses... Cela me donne très envie de savoir ce que sera la suite.
russian: Между нами столько всего произошло... И я уже жду, что будет дальше.
bulgarian: So much has happened... It makes me excited about what's to come.

english: First I need to focus on finishing my cookbook...
french: D'abord, je dois me concentrer pour terminer mon livre de cuisine...
russian: Для начала мне надо собраться с силами и дописать кулинарную книгу...
bulgarian: First I need to focus on finishing my cookbook...

english: And after that, maybe a farm-to-table seasonal experience at the Inn?
french: Et ensuite, pourquoi pas organiser des repas à l'auberge, de la fourchette à l'assiette, en fonction des saisons ?
russian: Затем, возможно, подготовить для трактира сезонное меню из фермерских продуктов?
bulgarian: And after that, maybe a farm-to-table seasonal experience at the Inn?

english: Well, whatever we do next, however much time might pass...
french: Quoi que nous fassions par la suite, quel que soit le temps qui passe...
russian: Впрочем, не важно, чем мы будем заниматься и сколько времени пройдёт...
bulgarian: Well, whatever we do next, however much time might pass...

english: As long as we're in it together, I know it's going to be great.
french: Du moment que nous sommes ensemble, je sais que ce sera fantastique.
russian: Я уверена: пока мы вместе, мы будем счастливы.
bulgarian: As long as we're in it together, I know it's going to be great.

english: It's amazing how time flies, huh?
french: C'est incroyable à quel point le temps file, non ?
russian: Удивительно, как летит время!
bulgarian: It's amazing how time flies, huh?

english: Growing up, my parents always told me stories from their days as traveling musicians.
french: Pendant toute mon enfance, mes parents m'ont raconté des histoires sur l'époque où ils tournaient avec leur groupe.
russian: Когда я была маленькая, родители рассказывали мне истории из своих музыкальных путешествий.
bulgarian: Growing up, my parents always told me stories from their days as traveling musicians.

english: They'd move from town to town, playing shows at each inn as they went.
french: Ils allaient de ville en ville et donnaient des concerts dans les auberges.
russian: Они ездили из города в город и выступали в каждом встречном трактире.
bulgarian: They'd move from town to town, playing shows at each inn as they went.

english: Some inns were smaller and more run down than others...
french: Elles n'étaient pas toujours très grandes ou en très bon état.
russian: Иногда трактиры попадались небольшие и ветхие...
bulgarian: Some inns were smaller and more run down than others...

english: But even in the poorest villages, there would always be a smiling face and a hot meal waiting to welcome them.
french: Mais même dans les villages les plus pauvres, on les accueillait toujours avec un sourire et un bon repas chaud.
russian: Но даже в самых бедных деревнях их встречали улыбкой и горячим ужином.
bulgarian: But even in the poorest villages, there would always be a smiling face and a hot meal waiting to welcome them.

english: Warming their weary hearts and stomachs after a long day on the road.
french: Ça leur réchauffait le cœur et le ventre après une longue journée sur la route.
russian: Это помогало им согреть сердце и живот после долгого дня в пути.
bulgarian: Warming their weary hearts and stomachs after a long day on the road.

english: I think maybe that's what inspired my love for cooking...
french: C'est peut-être pour ça que j'aime autant la cuisine...
russian: Я думаю, возможно, это вдохновило меня полюбить кулинарию...
bulgarian: I think maybe that's what inspired my love for cooking...

english: It's such a tangible way of showing care for another person.
french: C'est une manière si concrète de prendre soin des autres.
russian: Это такой ощутимый способ проявить заботу о человеке.
bulgarian: It's such a tangible way of showing care for another person.

english: I hope the Sleeping Dragon Inn will always be a place that a traveler can call home, if even just for a night.
french: J'espère que l'auberge du Dragon qui dort sera toujours un lieu où les voyageurs se sentiront chez eux, même si ce n'est qu'une nuit.
russian: Надеюсь, в трактире «Спящий дракон» путешественники всегда смогут найти свой дом, пускай и на одну ночь.
bulgarian: I hope the Sleeping Dragon Inn will always be a place that a traveler can call home, if even just for a night.

english: Want to hear a secret, [Ari]?
french: Tu veux que je te dise un secret, [Ari] ?
russian: Хочешь, скажу кое-что по секрету, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Want to hear a secret, [Ari]?

english: It's amazing to be surrounded by folks who look out for you.
french: C'est fantastique d'être entourée de personnes qui prennent soin de toi.
russian: Это потрясающе, когда все люди вокруг о тебе заботятся.
bulgarian: It's amazing to be surrounded by folks who look out for you.

english: And you can taste test for me anytime!
french: Et tu pourras goûter mes plats à tout instant !
russian: А ты можешь дегустировать для меня, когда захочешь!
bulgarian: And you can taste test for me anytime!

english: But I didn't realize what a difference it would make to have someone truly share in my dreams...
french: Mais je ne pensais pas qu'avoir à mes côtés une personne qui partage vraiment mes rêves changerait à ce point les choses...
russian: Но я и не знала, как важно, оказывается, иметь человека, с которым я могу разделить свои мечты...
bulgarian: But I didn't realize what a difference it would make to have someone truly share in my dreams...

english: Not until you moved to town.
french: Jusqu'à ton arrivée en ville.
russian:
Пока ты не

приехали

приехалаприехалприехало к нам в город.
bulgarian: Not until you moved to town.

english: It makes me so happy!
french: Et j'en suis très heureuse !
russian: Я так счастлива!
bulgarian: It makes me so happy!

english: Me too! I'll always enjoy cooking!
french: Moi aussi ! J'aimerai toujours cuisiner !
russian: Я тоже! Никогда не устану готовить!
bulgarian: Me too! I'll always enjoy cooking!

english: Me too! I'll always enjoy eating your food!
french: Moi aussi ! J'aimerai toujours déguster tes petits plats !
russian: Я тоже! Никогда не устану есть твою еду!
bulgarian: Me too! I'll always enjoy eating your food!

english: I'm so glad [Ari]!
french: Je suis si contente, [Ari] !
russian: Как я рада, [Ari]!
bulgarian: I'm so glad [Ari]!

english: Let's keep helping each other get better and better.
french: On va s'entraider pour faire toujours mieux.
russian: Давай будем помогать друг другу становиться лучше.
bulgarian: Let's keep helping each other get better and better.

english: I'll taste test for you anytime you need it!
french: Je me ferai un plaisir de goûter tes préparations !
russian: Я могу для тебя дегустировать, когда захочешь!
bulgarian: I'll taste test for you anytime you need it!

english: I'm so glad [Ari]!
french: Je suis si contente, [Ari] !
russian: Как я рада, [Ari]!
bulgarian: I'm so glad [Ari]!

english: I'm so glad [Ari]!
french: Je suis si contente, [Ari] !
russian: Как я рада, [Ari]!
bulgarian: I'm so glad [Ari]!

english: I promise I'll keep working hard at it.
french: C'est promis. Je continuerai à cuisiner de tout mon cœur.
russian: Обещаю, что продолжу развивать свои навыки!
bulgarian: I promise I'll keep working hard at it.

french: C'est promis. Je continuerai à cuisiner de tout mon cœur.
russian: Обещаю, что продолжу развивать свои навыки!
bulgarian: I promise I'll keep working hard at it.

english: I loved growing up in a cozy little place like Mistria.
french: J'ai adoré grandir dans une petite ville tranquille comme Mistria.
russian: В таком маленьком уютном местечке, как Мистрия, у меня было счастливое детство.
bulgarian: I loved growing up in a cozy little place like Mistria.

english: It's funny... I was just thinking about the first time you came to the Inn.
french: C'est drôle... Je repensais à ta première visite à l'auberge.
russian:
Забавно... Я как раз вспоминала тот раз, когда ты впервые

пришлапришёлпришло в трактир.

english: And that first Friday night you joined the festivities.
french: À la première soirée du vendredi que tu as passée avec nous.
russian:
И первую пятницу, когда ты

присоединились

присоединиласьприсоединилсяприсоединилось к веселью.
bulgarian: And that first Friday night you joined the festivities.

english: It all feels so long ago, doesn't it? It's hard to imagine this place without you.
french: J'ai l'impression que c'était il y a une éternité. J'ai du mal à imaginer cet endroit sans toi.
russian: Кажется, это было так давно. Трудно представить это место без тебя.
bulgarian: It all feels so long ago, doesn't it? It's hard to imagine this place without you.

english: Here, let me mix you up something tasty... for old time's sake!
french: Laisse-moi te préparer un petit quelque chose... en souvenir du temps qui passe !
russian: Давай налью тебе что-нибудь вкусненькое... За добрую память!
bulgarian: Here, let me mix you up something tasty... for old time's sake!

english: Hey [Ari]!
french: Salut, [Ari] !
russian: Привет, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]!

english: Now Mines forage is always in stock, and you're regularly finding exciting new ingredients, too!
french: Maintenant, on a refait les réserves et tu nous trouves régulièrement de nouveaux ingrédients.
russian: Теперь растения из шахт всегда в наличии. К тому же ты постоянно находишь новые необычные ингредиенты!
bulgarian: Now Mines forage is always in stock, and you're regularly finding exciting new ingredients, too!

english: I'm so happy that we've reconnected with that aspect of our culinary tradition.
french: Je suis si contente qu'on ait pu renouer avec cette facette de nos traditions culinaires.
russian: Я так рада, что мы не утратили эту часть наших кулинарных традиций.
bulgarian: I'm so happy that we've reconnected with that aspect of our culinary tradition.

english: And it's been fun trying my hand at these old recipes again. Like this one!
french: En plus, je m'amuse comme une folle à tester ces vieilles recettes. Comme celle-ci !
russian: А ещё увлекательно воссоздавать эти старые рецепты. Вот этот, например!
bulgarian: And it's been fun trying my hand at these old recipes again. Like this one!

english: It's hard to believe how long we went without access to ingredients from the Mines, after the earthquake.
french: Difficile d'imaginer que suite au tremblement de terre, on ait été si longtemps privés de produits provenant des mines.
russian: Трудно представить, как долго нам приходилось обходиться без ингредиентов из шахт из-за землетрясения.
bulgarian: It's hard to believe how long we went without access to ingredients from the Mines, after the earthquake.

english: Mom told me it was named by her great great grandpa.
french: Maman m'a dit que c'était en hommage à son arrière-grand-père.
russian: Мама говорит, что его назвал её прапрапрадед.
bulgarian: Mom told me it was named by her great great grandpa.

english: But it's been generations, so I'm sure the story has changed over the years.
french: Mais cela remonte à quelques générations. L'histoire a dû changer au fil des années.
russian: Но с тех пор сменилось несколько поколений — наверняка рассказ за эти годы успел измениться.
bulgarian: But it's been generations, so I'm sure the story has changed over the years.

english: Even if it turns out it wasn't true... it's fun to think about, isn't it?
french: Et même si tout était inventé... c'est amusant comme idée, non ?
russian: Даже если окажется, что это неправда... Всё равно приятно об этом думать.
bulgarian: Even if it turns out it wasn't true... it's fun to think about, isn't it?

english: Wouldn't that be amazing?
french: Ce serait incroyable, non ?
russian: Вот бы здорово было, правда?
bulgarian: Wouldn't that be amazing?

english: Some of the forest around Mistria is so impenetrable... it really feels like anything could be out there.
french: La forêt entourant Mistria est tellement dense. On a l'impression qu'elle pourrait abriter tout et n'importe quoi.
russian: Вокруг Мистрии есть совершенно неплроходимые леса... Кажется, будто в них правда может скрываться что угодно.
bulgarian: Some of the forest around Mistria is so impenetrable... it really feels like anything could be out there.

english: It's been generations, so I'm sure the story has changed over the years. Maybe it never even happened!
french: Ça remonte à quelques générations. Je suis sûre que l'histoire a dû changer au fil des années. Ce n'est peut-être même jamais arrivé !
russian: Но с тех пор сменилось несколько поколений — наверняка рассказ за эти годы успел измениться. Может, этого и не было никогда!
bulgarian: It's been generations, so I'm sure the story has changed over the years. Maybe it never even happened!

english: Or maybe there's still a slumbering dragon out there even now!
french: Ou peut-être qu'un dragon dort quelque part dans la forêt en ce moment même !
russian: А может, где-то там до сих пор спит дракон!
bulgarian: Or maybe there's still a slumbering dragon out there even now!

english: The story goes that he visited the $Deep Woods$ one day, and got lost after he strayed from his usual path.
french: L'histoire veut qu'un jour, il soit allé se promener à $Boissombre$ et qu'il se soit perdu après s'être écarté du sentier.
russian: По её словам, однажды он шёл по $Глубокой чаще$, сошёл с привычной дороги и заблудился.
bulgarian: The story goes that he visited the $Deep Woods$ one day, and got lost after he strayed from his usual path.

english: He wandered among dense trees for hours, searching for the path home.
french: Il aurait erré des heures durant dans des sous-bois épais, à essayer de retrouver son chemin.
russian: Он несколько часов бродил среди густых деревьев в поисках тропинки к дому.
bulgarian: He wandered among dense trees for hours, searching for the path home.

english: Finally, he came across some old ruins in a clearing. The sun was setting, so he decided to shelter there until the next day.
french: Finalement, il serait arrivé à un amas de ruines dans une clairière. Le soleil étant près de se coucher, il aurait décidé de s'y abriter pour la nuit.
russian: Наконец он вышел к поляне со старинными руинами. Солнце уже садилось, и он решил там переночевать.
bulgarian: Finally, he came across some old ruins in a clearing. The sun was setting, so he decided to shelter there until the next day.
