russian: Иногда у Мэрри в лавке появляется мебель дяди Ландена... у меня не поднимается рука сказать ему, что он теперь считается «винтажным».
bulgarian: Every once in a while one of Uncle Landen's pieces ends up in Merri's shop... I don't have the heart to tell him he's vintage.

english: Merri stops by the woodshop every so often, when she's got something unusual she wants an opinion on. It's always interesting.
french: Merri passe de temps à autre à la menuiserie. Le plus souvent, c'est quand elle veut un avis sur un objet plutôt inhabituel. C'est toujours très intéressant.
russian: Мэрри заглядывает в мастерскую время от времени, если находит что-то необычное и хочет совета. У нее всегда интересные вопросы.
bulgarian: Merri stops by the woodshop every so often, when she's got something unusual she wants an opinion on. It's always interesting.

english: Fortunes are cool, [Ari]... they give you something to think about, or help you reframe something you were already thinking about.
bulgarian: Fortunes are cool, [Ari]... they give you something to think about, or help you reframe something you were already thinking about.

english: With Stillwell's fortunes, that usually means thinking about darkness and stuff... but like, in a positive way.
bulgarian: With Stillwell's fortunes, that usually means thinking about darkness and stuff... but like, in a positive way.

english: "You came from the city to the grove, and the grove is where you'll find yourself". Stillwell's fortunes get kinda deep, [Ari]...
bulgarian: "You came from the city to the grove, and the grove is where you'll find yourself". Stillwell's fortunes get kinda deep, [Ari]...

english: I asked Stillwell to do a money fortune for March, and he said "a fool is soon parted from his gold"... maybe I'll keep that one to myself.
bulgarian: I asked Stillwell to do a money fortune for March, and he said "a fool is soon parted from his gold"... maybe I'll keep that one to myself.

english: March only ever gets love fortunes from Stillwell... he's too embarrassed to admit it, though.
bulgarian: March only ever gets love fortunes from Stillwell... he's too embarrassed to admit it, though.

english: I just wish he'd be a big deal outside of earshot...
french: Si seulement il pouvait être plus aimable...
russian: Вот только лучше бы он важничал где-нибудь подальше...
bulgarian: I just wish he'd be a big deal outside of earshot...

english: It's a pretty big deal that Taliferro is here in Mistria, right? Back in the Capital, it sounded like he was a big deal, too...
french: Le fait que Taliferro soit à Mistria, c'est bien pour la ville, non ? Quand j'étais à la capitale, j'avais l'impression que c'était quelqu'un d'important.
russian: Приезд Талиферро для Мистрии — важное событие, так? И в столице он, кажется, тоже был важной шишкой...
bulgarian: It's a pretty big deal that Taliferro is here in Mistria, right? Back in the Capital, it sounded like he was a big deal, too...

english: I wonder what his story is...
french: Je me demande comment ça se fait...
russian: Интересно, что у него за история...
bulgarian: I wonder what his story is...

english: Oh well! None of my business.
french: Mais bon, ça ne me regarde pas !
russian: Впрочем, это не моё дело!
bulgarian: Oh well! None of my business.

english: Taliferro is some sort of nobility, isn't he? Usually aristocrats don't have careers like challenge organizer or professional chef.
french: Taliferro est un aristocrate, non ? Normalement, ces gens-là ne sont pas chefs et n'organisent pas de concours.
russian: Талиферро вроде бы какой-то дворянин. Организатор конкурсов и шеф-повар — необычные профессии для аристократа.
bulgarian: Taliferro is some sort of nobility, isn't he? Usually aristocrats don't have careers like challenge organizer or professional chef.

english: I'm a pretty good baker, but I'd like to keep my self-esteem intact, thanks very much!
french: Je cuisine plutôt bien, alors je préfère éviter qu'on me sape le moral !
russian: У меня весьма приличная выпечка, но нет, спасибо, я бы хотел сохранить самооценку!
bulgarian: I'm a pretty good baker, but I'd like to keep my self-esteem intact, thanks very much!

english: I think I'll cut out from Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$ this week...
french: Je crois que je vais passer le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro cette semaine...
russian: Думаю, я на этой неделе откажусь от участия в $смотре блюд$ Талиферро...
bulgarian: I think I'll cut out from Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$ this week...

english: If he sees a challenge, he's going to want to win it!
french: S'il y a un défi à relever, il fera tout pour le réussir.
russian: Если ему бросить вызов, он будет идти к победе!
bulgarian: If he sees a challenge, he's going to want to win it!

english: I really admire March's ability to keep re-entering Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, no matter how many times he fails...
french: J'admire March et sa persévérance, alors qu'il n'arrête pas de perdre le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro ?
russian: Я уважаю Марта за то, что, несмотря на все провалы, он продолжает участвовать в $смотрах блюд$ Талиферро...
bulgarian: I really admire March's ability to keep re-entering Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, no matter how many times he fails...

english: Green hair might suit me, [Ari]. What do you think?
french: Tu crois que les cheveux verts, ça m'irait, [Ari] ?
russian: Как думаешь, [Ari], мне может пойти зелёный цвет волос?
bulgarian: Green hair might suit me, [Ari]. What do you think?

english: I like your haircut, [Ari]. It's so you.
french: J'aime bien ta coiffure, [Ari]. Elle te va très bien.
russian: Мне нравится твоя причёска, [Ari]. Прямо ты.
bulgarian: I like your haircut, [Ari]. It's so you.

english: Vera always gets my fade juuust right.
french: Vera me fait toujours un dégradé parfait.
russian: Вера всегда идеально делает мне фейд.
bulgarian: Vera always gets my fade juuust right.

english: What if I went red to match March? Might think I'm stealing his thunder, though.
french: Et si je me faisais teindre en roux comme March ? Non, il risquerait de penser que je cherche à lui voler la vedette.
russian: А если покраситься в красный, как Март? Хотя, может, подумает, что я у него внимание отбираю.
bulgarian: What if I went red to match March? Might think I'm stealing his thunder, though.

english: Unrelated, but how much of a nuisance does someone have to be for Nora to cancel their vendor's license?
french: D'ailleurs, je me demande à quel point un marchand devrait être pénible pour que Nora lui supprime sa licence ?
russian: К другой теме: насколько нужно насолить Норе, чтобы она отозвала лицензию торговца?
bulgarian: Unrelated, but how much of a nuisance does someone have to be for Nora to cancel their vendor's license?

english: I heard... rumors about Wheedle in the Capital. I guess he finally made his way to Mistria.
french: J'avais beaucoup entendu parler de Wheedle à la capitale. On dirait qu'au bout du compte, il s'est rabattu sur Mistria.
russian: Я слышал... слухи при Хлюста в столице. Так значит, он наконец добрался и до Мистрии.
bulgarian: I heard... rumors about Wheedle in the Capital. I guess he finally made his way to Mistria.

english: Does he deserve your money, though? You have to answer that one for yourself.
french: Mais mérite-t-il notre argent ? C'est une question que l'on doit se poser.
russian: Но заслуживает ли он твоих денег? На этот вопрос каждый отвечает за себя.
bulgarian: Does he deserve your money, though? You have to answer that one for yourself.

english: Don't like admitting it, but Wheedle's $Deluxe Chests$ are the real deal. They're well-made and roomy.
french: Ça me coûte de l'admettre, mais les $coffres haut de gamme$ de Wheedle valent le détour. Ils sont de bonne facture et spacieux.
russian: Не хочется признавать, но $элитные сундуки$ у Хлюста правда качественные. Вместительные и крепко сколочены.
bulgarian: Don't like admitting it, but Wheedle's $Deluxe Chests$ are the real deal. They're well-made and roomy.

english: Just so you know, not everyone from the Capital is like them! Most of us are cool!
french: Mais rassure-toi, tout le monde n'est pas comme eux là-bas ! La plupart des habitants de la capitale sont des gens sympas !
russian:
Чтобы ты

знали

зналазналзнало: не все в столице такие! Большинство нормальные!
bulgarian: Just so you know, not everyone from the Capital is like them! Most of us are cool!

english: Between Wheedle and Taliferro, we sure are getting some odd birds from the Capital, huh?
french: Entre Wheedle et Taliferro, la capitale nous envoie de drôles d'oiseaux, hein ?
russian: Судя по Хлюсту и Талиферро, из столицы нам присылают чудаковатых людей.
bulgarian: Between Wheedle and Taliferro, we sure are getting some odd birds from the Capital, huh?

english: Didn't he get in trouble for selling defective oxcarts? Don't take my word for it, maybe I'm misremembering...
french: Il n'avait pas eu des ennuis pour avoir vendu des chars à bœufs défectueux ? J'ai un doute. Je confonds peut-être...
russian: Это не он случайно попал в переделку из-за продажи сломанных повозок? Но можешь не верить, я мог перепутать...
bulgarian: Didn't he get in trouble for selling defective oxcarts? Don't take my word for it, maybe I'm misremembering...

english: Now that I think about it, I'm sure I've seen Wheedle in the Capital before...
french: En y réfléchissant, je suis sûr d'avoir déjà croisé Wheedle à la capitale avant...
russian: Я теперь задумался: кажется, я раньше встречал Хлюста в столице...
bulgarian: Now that I think about it, I'm sure I've seen Wheedle in the Capital before...

english: You could have a song for every room of your house!
french: Tu pourrais avoir une chanson pour chaque pièce de ta maison.
russian: Можно для каждой комнаты в доме подобрать свою музыку!
bulgarian: You could have a song for every room of your house!

english: Can you believe how innovative the $Song Crystal$ Zorel sells are?
french: Le $cristal musical$ que vend Zorel est une véritable innovation.
russian: Ты представляешь какое чудо техники эти $поющие кристаллы$ у Зорель?
bulgarian: Can you believe how innovative the $Song Crystal$ Zorel sells are?

english: If I had a load of those, I could tile a whole roof!
french: Si j'en avais plein, je pourrais en recouvrir un toit entier !
russian: Вот бы мне побольше таких, я бы из них целую крышу сделал.
bulgarian: If I had a load of those, I could tile a whole roof!

english: I like the look of that $Dragon Scale$ at the Museum... it seems hard and durable.
french: J'aime l'aspect de cette $écaille de dragon$, au musée... Elle a l'air solide et durable.
russian: Мне нравится смотреть на $чешую дракона$ в музее... Вылядит твёрдо и очень надёжно.
bulgarian: I like the look of that $Dragon Scale$ at the Museum... it seems hard and durable.

english: I thought they opened a bird wing.
french: J'ai cru qu'ils avaient ouvert une aile dédiée aux oiseaux.
russian: Думал, в музее открыли отдел для птиц.
bulgarian: I thought they opened a bird wing.

english: Turns out a Forest Perch is a fish. That's cool, I guess.
french: Mais une perche forestière, c'est un poisson. Ça a aussi son charme.
russian: Оказалось, это лучепёрая рыба — $лесной окунь$. Ну, тоже круто, наверное.
bulgarian: Turns out a Forest Perch is a fish. That's cool, I guess.

english: I heard there was a $Forest Perch$ over at the Museum, so I raced over.
french: J'ai entendu dire qu'il y avait une $perche forestière$ au musée, alors j'ai accouru.
russian: Я услышал, что в музее какие-то лучепёрые, и прибежал посмотерть на пёрышки.
bulgarian: I heard there was a $Forest Perch$ over at the Museum, so I raced over.

english: Talks almost as much as my Uncle Landen.
french: Il parle presque autant qu'oncle Landen.
russian: Говорит почти столько же, сколько мой дядя Ланден.
bulgarian: Talks almost as much as my Uncle Landen.

english: Gotta say, that $Muttering Cube$ at the Museum is pretty unsettling.
french: Je trouve ce $cube aux murmures$ du musée vraiment très fatigant.
russian: Надо сказать, этот $бормочущий кубик$ в музее немного пугает.
bulgarian: Gotta say, that $Muttering Cube$ at the Museum is pretty unsettling.

english: I'd never seen a butterfly so big I mistook it for a bird before!
french: Je n'avais encore jamais vu de papillon si gros que je l'ai d'abord pris pour un oiseau.
russian: Никогда ещё не видел бабочку таких размеров, чтобы можно было принять за птицу!
bulgarian: I'd never seen a butterfly so big I mistook it for a bird before!

english: That $Queen's Birdwing$ at the Museum is really something...
french: Ces $ailes de reine$, au musée, c'est vraiment quelque chose...
russian: $Королевская птицекрылка$ в музее — это просто нечто...
bulgarian: That $Queen's Birdwing$ at the Museum is really something...

english: Is it a rock, or is it wood? I can't tell!
french: Elle est en pierre ou en bois ? Je n'arrive pas à le savoir !
russian: Он всё-таки камень? Или всё-таки дерево? Я так и не понял.
bulgarian: Is it a rock, or is it wood? I can't tell!

english: I was at the Museum and I gotta say, that $Rockroot$ has me stumped.
french: J'étais au musée l'autre jour, et la $racine de roche$ qui y est exposée m'a laissé perplexe.
russian: Был в музее. Скажу честно, этот $камнекорень$ меня сбил с толку.
bulgarian: I was at the Museum and I gotta say, that $Rockroot$ has me stumped.

english: I think it's even more ancient than Uncle Landen's!
french: Il doit être encore plus vieux que celui d'oncle Landen !
russian: Похоже, даже старше молотка дяди Ландена.
bulgarian: I think it's even more ancient than Uncle Landen's!

english: That $Vintage Hammer$ at the Museum might be the oldest hammer I've ever seen.
french: Je crois que le $marteau rétro$ du musée est le plus vieil outil que j'aie jamais vu.
russian: Этот $старинный молоток$ в музее, наверное, самый древний из всех, что я видел.
bulgarian: That $Vintage Hammer$ at the Museum might be the oldest hammer I've ever seen.

english: Let's make the best of it, okay?
french: Profitons au maximum de la journée, hein ?
russian: Желаю тебе провести день с пользой.
bulgarian: Let's make the best of it, okay?

english: [Ari], good morning.
french: Bien le bonjour, [Ari].
russian: [Ari], доброе утро.
bulgarian: [Ari], good morning.

english: Love that fit on you, [Ari].
french: J'adore ta tenue, [Ari].
russian: Обожаю этот твой наряд, [Ari].
bulgarian: Love that fit on you, [Ari].

english: Maybe we could even pick a project to do together.
french: On pourrait même trouver un projet à faire ensemble.
russian: Может, мы даже займёмся совместным проектом?
bulgarian: Maybe we could even pick a project to do together.

english: If you're ever looking for something fun to do, stop by the shop!
french: Si jamais tu as envie de faire quelque chose de sympa, passe à l'atelier !
russian: Если захочешь поделать что-нибудь интересное, заходи в мастерскую!
bulgarian: If you're ever looking for something fun to do, stop by the shop!

english: Well, as long as I get to spend some of it with you, I guess it's alright.
french: Enfin, tant que je passe du temps avec toi, peu importe le reste.
russian: Впрочем, если я хоть часть времени проведу с тобой, это не страшно.
bulgarian: Well, as long as I get to spend some of it with you, I guess it's alright.

english: Where did the day go? I can't believe it's the afternoon already.
french: La journée a filé à une vitesse ! Je n'arrive pas à croire que ce soit déjà l'après-midi.
russian: Почему день так быстро проходит? Поверить не могу, что уже вечереет.
bulgarian: Where did the day go? I can't believe it's the afternoon already.

english: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.
french: Ça te dirait d'y aller ensemble, un de ces jours ? On s'amuserait bien, j'en suis sûr.
russian: Хочешь, как-нибудь сходим вместе? Уверен, будет весело.
bulgarian: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.

english: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.
french: J'ai eu pas mal de chance en observant les oiseaux, ces derniers temps.
russian: В последнее время у меня весьма успешные наблюдения за птицами.
bulgarian: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.

english: Was just thinking how I wanted to hang out with you.
french: J'étais justement en train de me dire que ça me ferait plaisir de faire quelque chose avec toi.
russian: Я как раз думал, что хочу с тобой встретиться.
bulgarian: Was just thinking how I wanted to hang out with you.

english: Wanna chat?
french: Tu as envie de discuter ?
russian: Хочешь поболтать?
bulgarian: Wanna chat?

english: A nice, full day. Wanna hear about it?
french: La journée a été bien remplie. Tu veux que je te raconte ?
russian: Это был хороший, насыщенный день. Хочешь послушать?
bulgarian: A nice, full day. Wanna hear about it?

english: I'd love to hear all about yours too.
french: Et j'aimerais beaucoup que tu me racontes la tienne, aussi.
russian: Я с радостью послушаю, что было у тебя.
bulgarian: I'd love to hear all about yours too.

english: Hey [Ari], good evening!
french: Hé, bonsoir [Ari] !
russian: Эй, [Ari], добрый вечер!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], good evening!

english: Unless you want to hang out. I've always got time for you!
french: À moins que tu aies envie de faire quelque chose. J'ai toujours du temps pour toi.
russian: Если, конечно, ты не хочешь поболтать. Для тебя у меня всегда найдётся время!
bulgarian: Unless you want to hang out. I've always got time for you!

english: Busy day tomorrow, I should get to sleep soon...
french: Une grosse journée m'attend demain, je ne devrais pas tarder à aller au lit.
russian: Мне скоро пора ложиться: много планов на завтра...
bulgarian: Busy day tomorrow, I should get to sleep soon...

english: Can't wait to show you when they're done!
french: J'ai hâte de te montrer tout ça quand ça sera terminé !
russian: Скоро доделаю, уже не терпится тебе показать!
bulgarian: Can't wait to show you when they're done!

english: Had a chance to work on some blueprints for a new project today.
french: J'ai eu l'idée d'un nouveau projet, aujourd'hui.
russian: Недавно выпала возможность поработать над чертежами нового проекта.
bulgarian: Had a chance to work on some blueprints for a new project today.

english: Let's make the best of it, okay?
french: Profitons au maximum de la journée, hein ?
russian: Желаю тебе провести день с пользой.
bulgarian: Let's make the best of it, okay?

english: [Ari], good morning.
french: Bien le bonjour, [Ari].
russian: [Ari], доброе утро.
bulgarian: [Ari], good morning.

english: Love that fit on you, [Ari].
french: J'adore ta tenue, [Ari].
russian: Обожаю этот твой наряд, [Ari].
bulgarian: Love that fit on you, [Ari].

french: On pourrait même trouver un projet à faire ensemble.
russian: Может, мы даже займёмся совместным проектом?
bulgarian: Maybe we could even pick a project to do together.

french: Si jamais tu as envie de faire quelque chose de sympa, passe à l'atelier !
russian: Если захочешь поделать что-нибудь интересное, заходи в мастерскую!

russian: Впрочем, если я хоть часть времени проведу с тобой, то это не страшно.
bulgarian: Well, as long as I get to spend some of it with you, I guess it's alright.

russian: Почему день так быстро проходит? Поверить не могу, что уже вечереет.
bulgarian: Where did the day go? I can't believe it's the afternoon already.

english: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.
french: Ça te dirait d'y aller ensemble, un de ces jours ? On s'amuserait bien, j'en suis sûr.
russian: Хочешь, как-нибудь сходим вместе? Уверен, будет весело.
bulgarian: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.

english: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.
french: J'ai eu pas mal de chance en observant les oiseaux, ces derniers temps.
russian: В последнее время у меня весьма успешные наблюдения за птицами.
bulgarian: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.

english: We should plan to go out on a date sometime soon.
french: On devrait prendre du temps pour un rendez-vous en amoureux, un de ces jours.
russian: Давай запланируем свидание на ближайшее время.
bulgarian: We should plan to go out on a date sometime soon.

english: I know we're both busy but...
french: Je sais qu'on a beaucoup à faire, tous les deux, mais...
russian: Я знаю, что мы оба обычно заняты, но...
bulgarian: I know we're both busy but...

french: Quelle journée bien remplie ! Tu veux que je te raconte ?
russian: Это был хороший, насыщенный день. Хочешь послушать?
bulgarian: What a full day. Wanna hear about it?

french: Et j'aimerais beaucoup que tu me racontes la tienne, aussi.
russian: Я с радостью послушаю, что было у тебя.

english: Hey [Ari], good evening!
french: Hé, bonsoir [Ari] !
russian: Эй, [Ari], добрый вечер!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], good evening!

english: Unless... you want to hang out. I've always got time for you!
french: À moins que tu aies envie de faire quelque chose. J'ai toujours du temps pour toi.
russian: Если, конечно... ты не хочешь поболтать. Для тебя у меня всегда найдётся время!

bulgarian: Haha! You surprised me!

english: Okay, yeah. I can do this.
french: Bon, d'accord. Je peux y arriver.
russian: Что ж, ладно. Попробую ещё.
bulgarian: Okay, yeah. I can do this.

english: Hey, how about you and me go somewhere real quiet...
french: Hé, ça vous dirait de venir avec moi dans un endroit tranquille...
russian: Эй, может, найдём тихое местечко...
bulgarian: Hey, how about you and me go somewhere real quiet...

english: We can talk about... um.
french: On pourrait parler de... hum.
russian: Сядем вдвоём и поболтаем про... эм...
bulgarian: We can talk about... um.

english: Seasonal bird migration?
french: Des oiseaux migrateurs ?
russian: Сезонные миграции птиц?
bulgarian: Seasonal bird migration?

english: Let... let me get a do-over.
french: Attends... Je recommence.
russian: Ладно... Попытаюсь ещё раз.
bulgarian: Let... let me get a do-over.

english: Hey... Don't think we've ever met before. You come here often?
french: Salut, vous. Je ne crois pas qu'on se connaisse. Vous venez souvent ici ?
russian: Эй, ты. Мы, кажется, не знакомы. Часто здесь бываешь?
bulgarian: Hey... Don't think we've ever met before. You come here often?

english: But I can't wait to get old with you.
french: Il me tarde d'être un petit vieux.
russian: Мне не терпится постареть вместе с тобой.
bulgarian: But I can't wait to get old with you.

english: I want to know that [Ari] too, and all the [Ari]s in between then and now.
french: J'ai envie de connaître <she>celle</she><he>celui</he><they>cellui</they> que tu seras et <she>toutes</she><he>tous</he><they>tous·tes</they> les [Ari] entre deux.
russian:
Я хочу знать, как выглядит [Ari] в старости, и

каждые

каждаякаждыйкаждое [Ari] посередине.
bulgarian: I want to know that [Ari] too, and all the [Ari]s in between then and now.

english: And you'll get to know all the different versions of me from now on, too.
french: Et inversement, tu connaîtras toutes les versions de moi aussi.
russian: А ты сможешь познакомиться со всеми версиями меня. Начиная с нынешнего.
bulgarian: And you'll get to know all the different versions of me from now on, too.

english: Man... I can't wait!
french: Qu'est-ce que j'ai hâte !
russian: Ах... Уже не терпится!
bulgarian: Man... I can't wait!

english: This is gonna sound weird...
french: Ça va te paraître étrange, mais...
russian: Это может прозвучать странно, но...
bulgarian: This is gonna sound weird...

english: I've got a whole routine these days... repairs around town, minding the shop, filling Adeline's work orders...
french: Mes journées sont bien remplies en ce moment... entre les réparations en ville, la boutique et les tâches que me confie Adeline...
russian: У меня уже наладилась рутина... Ремонт в городе, работа в мастерской, выполнение заказов от Аделины...
bulgarian: I've got a whole routine these days... repairs around town, minding the shop, filling Adeline's work orders...

english: I guess I've really settled into life in Mistria. That's nice.
french: Je crois que je me suis bien intégré à la vie de Mistria. C'est bien.
russian: Кажется, я, наконец, освоился в Мистрии. Это приятно.
bulgarian: I guess I've really settled into life in Mistria. That's nice.

english: I mean, there's no real settling in when you've got an Uncle Landen. He keeps things interesting.
french: Et puis, avec oncle Landen, on n'a jamais le temps de s'ennuyer. Tout est intéressant avec lui.
russian: Конечно, окончательно обосноваться с дядей Ланденом не получится. У него всегда какие-нибудь необычные идеи.
bulgarian: I mean, there's no real settling in when you've got an Uncle Landen. He keeps things interesting.

english: But... I'd say I've gotten pretty used to that, too.
french: Mais... je crois que je m'y suis habitué aussi.
russian: Но... Я бы сказал, что и к этому я тоже привык.
bulgarian: But... I'd say I've gotten pretty used to that, too.

english: I was thinking about our time together, and making the birdhouse, and everything we talked about...
french: Je repensais aux moments qu'on a passés, au nichoir qu'on a fabriqué et à tout ce dont on a parlé...
russian: Я размышлял, как мы проводили с тобой время, и про скворечник, и про всё, о чём мы говорили...
bulgarian: I was thinking about our time together, and making the birdhouse, and everything we talked about...

english: Turning a pile of materials into a barn or something... it feels good.
french: Transformer une pile de matériaux bruts en étable ou en poulailler... C'est gratifiant.
russian: Превратить кучу сырых материалов в хлев, например... Это приятно.
bulgarian: Turning a pile of materials into a barn or something... it feels good.

english: I wonder what my sisters would think if they saw me swinging a hammer around?
french: Je me demande ce que mes sœurs diraient si elles me voyaient avec mon marteau.
russian: Интересно, что бы сказали мои сёстры, если бы застали меня с молотком?
bulgarian: I wonder what my sisters would think if they saw me swinging a hammer around?

english: They're used to seeing me covered in flour.
french: Elles étaient habituées à me voir couvert de farine.
russian: Они-то привыкли, что у меня повсюду мука.
bulgarian: They're used to seeing me covered in flour.

english: Now you're covered in sawdust!
french: Maintenant, tu es couvert de sciure !
russian: А теперь у тебя повсюду опилки!
bulgarian: Now you're covered in sawdust!

english: I bet they'd be as impressed as I am.
french: Je parie qu'elles seraient impressionnées, comme moi.
russian: Наверняка они бы впечатлились, как и я.
bulgarian: I bet they'd be as impressed as I am.

english: The more things change, the more they stay the same, right?
french: Il faut que tout change pour que rien ne change, pas vrai ?
russian: Что-то меняется, а что-то остаётся прежним, да?
bulgarian: The more things change, the more they stay the same, right?

english: No matter what I do, it's always a battle to keep my clothes looking nice.
french: Quel que soit mon métier, je dois toujours me battre pour ne pas tacher mes vêtements.
russian: Что бы я ни делал, никак не выходит держать одежду чистой.
bulgarian: No matter what I do, it's always a battle to keep my clothes looking nice.

english: Haha, maybe... but they'd definitely tease me about it.
french: Ha ha, peut-être... mais je pense surtout qu'elles me taquineraient.
russian: Ха-ха, может быть... Но они бы точно начали дразниться.
bulgarian: Haha, maybe... but they'd definitely tease me about it.

english: Then they'd ask me to build stuff for them.
french: Et ensuite, elles me demanderaient de leur fabriquer quelque chose.
russian: А потом попросили бы им что-нибудь построить.
bulgarian: Then they'd ask me to build stuff for them.

english: New display shelf for bread, new cabinets for the pots and pans...
french: Un nouveau présentoir à pain, des placards pour les casseroles et les poêles...
russian: Новую витрину для хлеба, новые шкафчики для кастрюль и сковородок...
bulgarian: New display shelf for bread, new cabinets for the pots and pans...

english: Huh. Maybe I should write them and see if they need anything. A brother should help his sisters out, right?
french: Mmm, je devrais peut-être leur écrire pour savoir si elles ont besoin de quelque chose. Un frère se doit d'aider ses sœurs, non ?
russian: Хм. Возможно, пора им написать и спросить, не нужно ли им чего. Брат же должен помогать своим сёстрам?
bulgarian: Huh. Maybe I should write them and see if they need anything. A brother should help his sisters out, right?

english: I really like building stuff...
french: J'adore fabriquer des trucs...
russian: Мне правда нравится создавать вещи...
bulgarian: I really like building stuff...

english: It's about time I got some more denim, but I kind of want a lighter wash this time.
french: Il est temps que je me rachète un jeans, mais j'aimerais une couleur un peu plus claire cette fois.
russian: Пора бы мне разжиться новыми джинсами, но теперь я хочу оттенок посветлее.
bulgarian: It's about time I got some more denim, but I kind of want a lighter wash this time.

english: Hopefully Louis has something... otherwise I guess I'll put something on order with him.
french: J'espère que Louis aura ça en stock... sinon je devrai lui passer commande.
russian: Надеюсь, у Луи что-нибудь найдётся... Иначе, видимо, придётся делать у него заказ.
bulgarian: Hopefully Louis has something... otherwise I guess I'll put something on order with him.

english: You're really into fashion, aren't you?
french: Tu aimes vraiment la mode, hein ?
russian: Я смотрю, ты всерьёз увлекаешься модой!
bulgarian: You're really into fashion, aren't you?

english: Your wardrobe's so stylish.
french: Ta garde-robe est vraiment stylée.
russian: Ты всегда так стильно выглядишь.
bulgarian: Your wardrobe's so stylish.

english: Guilty as charged...
french: Oui, j'avoue...
russian: Признаю свою вину!
bulgarian: Guilty as charged...

english: I'm not someone who puts fashion before comfort...
french: Je ne ferai pas passer le style avant le confort...
russian: Я не стану предпочитаь моду удобству...
bulgarian: I'm not someone who puts fashion before comfort...

english: But sometimes fashion is comfort, if that makes sense.
french: Mais parfois, la mode m'apporte une sorte de réconfort, si tu vois ce que je veux dire.
russian: Но иногда мода — и есть удобство, если ты понимаешь, о чём я.
bulgarian: But sometimes fashion is comfort, if that makes sense.

english: Oh, that's nice of you to say. I always thought that about you, actually.
french: Oh, c'est gentil de me dire ça. En fait, je me suis toujours dit la même chose pour la tienne.
russian: Ох, приятно слышать это от тебя. Вообще-то, я хотел сказать это о тебе.
bulgarian: Oh, that's nice of you to say. I always thought that about you, actually.

english: You've always got something that suits you.
french: Tu portes toujours des tenues qui te vont super bien.
russian: У тебя всегда есть подходящий наряд.
bulgarian: You've always got something that suits you.

english: I think that's pretty cool, [Ari].
french: Et je trouve ça super cool, [Ari].
russian: По-моему, это круто, [Ari].
bulgarian: I think that's pretty cool, [Ari].

english: Hey, [Ari]. I was just thinking about the next Saturday Market.
french: Salut, [Ari]. Je réfléchissais au prochain marché du samedi.
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Я тут разумываю насчёт предстоящего Субботнего базара.
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. I was just thinking about the next Saturday Market.

english: I've been thinking... when he grows up, he'll probably want to go to university in the Capital...
french: Je me disais... Il voudra certainement aller à l'université de la capitale quand il sera grand...
russian: И я подумал... Когда он вырастет, наверное, захочет поступить в столичный университет...
bulgarian: I've been thinking... when he grows up, he'll probably want to go to university in the Capital...

english: And, well... I was thinking 'bout how Uncle Landen put me up so I could come out to Mistria and learn a trade.
french: Et puis, j'ai repensé à oncle Landen qui m'a accueilli à Mistria pour que je puisse apprendre un métier.
russian: И кроме того... Я думал, как дядя Ланден пристроил меня у себя, чтобы я мог жить в Мистрии и осваивать ремесло.
bulgarian: And, well... I was thinking 'bout how Uncle Landen put me up so I could come out to Mistria and learn a trade.

english: I guess I want to pay that kindness forward. That's what community is about, right?
french: Je me dis que j'ai envie d'en faire autant. C'est l'idée quand on fait partie d'une communauté, non ?
russian: Видимо, я хочу передать добро дальше. Ведь это и есть настоящая взаимовыручка.
bulgarian: I guess I want to pay that kindness forward. That's what community is about, right?

english: Maybe one of my sisters could put him up. Or my aunt. Or one of my friends downtown...
french: Peut-être qu'une de mes sœurs pourra l'héberger. Ou ma tante. Ou un de mes amis...
russian: Может, получится пожить у одной из моих сестёр. Или у тёти. Или у одного из моих друзей в центре...
bulgarian: Maybe one of my sisters could put him up. Or my aunt. Or one of my friends downtown...

english: I should make time to talk to Josephine... bet I could set up some kind of boarding situation for him.
french: Il faudra que je trouve le temps d'en parler à Joséphine... Je suis sûr que je pourrais lui trouver une chambre chez quelqu'un.
russian: Надо бы мне выделить время и поговорить с Джозефиной... Наверняка получится устроить ему проживание.
bulgarian: I should make time to talk to Josephine... bet I could set up some kind of boarding situation for him.

english: What brought this on?
french: Comment ça t'est venu à l'esprit ?
russian: Почему ты вдруг об этом задумался?
bulgarian: What brought this on?

english: You know a lot of people in the Capital!
french: Tu en connais du monde à la capitale !
russian: У тебя так много знакомых в столице!
bulgarian: You know a lot of people in the Capital!

english: I like birds... but Luc REALLY likes insects.
french: Eh bien, j'aime les oiseaux... mais Luc aime VRAIMENT les insectes.
russian: Я люблю птиц... но Люк ПРАВДА обожает насекомых.
bulgarian: I like birds... but Luc REALLY likes insects.

english: And it's not just that he reads all about them... he makes his own observations, too.
french: Non seulement il lit tout ce qu'il trouve à leur sujet... mais il fait aussi ses propres observations.
russian: И он не просто много про них читает... Он ещё и проводит собственные наблюдения.
bulgarian: And it's not just that he reads all about them... he makes his own observations, too.

english: Hah, I like to keep in touch.
french: Ah, j'aime bien garder le contact.
russian: Хах, стараюсь поддерживать контакты.
bulgarian: Hah, I like to keep in touch.

english: And Luc... man, he REALLY likes insects.
french: Et Luc, lui... Il aime VRAIMENT les insectes.
russian: А Люк... слушай, он ПРАВДА обожает насекомых.
bulgarian: And Luc... man, he REALLY likes insects.

english: And it's not just that he reads all about them... he makes his own observations, too.
french: Non seulement il lit tout ce qu'il trouve à leur sujet... mais il fait aussi ses propres observations.
russian: И он не просто много про них читает... Он ещё и проводит собственные наблюдения.
bulgarian: And it's not just that he reads all about them... he makes his own observations, too.

english: He's really motivated... and if you pursue an education to the fullest, it can take you pretty far.
french: Il se donne à fond. Quand tu fais des études qui te passionnent, tu peux aller très loin.
russian: Он очень мотивированный... Если всерьёз заняться образованием, можно забраться весьма высоко.
bulgarian: He's really motivated... and if you pursue an education to the fullest, it can take you pretty far.

english: Luc sure does like bugs! He was showing me his favorite insects for hours the other day.
french: Luc adore les insectes ! Il m'a montré ses préférés pendant des heures l'autre jour.
russian: Люк просто обожает всяких жучков! Пару дней назад он мне несколько часов показывал своих любимых насекомых!
bulgarian: Luc sure does like bugs! He was showing me his favorite insects for hours the other day.

english: One of my sisters has her birthday in a few weeks, so I was trying to decide on a gift.
french: Ma sœur fête son anniversaire dans quelques semaines et j'essaie de lui trouver un cadeau.
russian: У одной из моих сестёр через пару недель день рождения, я пока раздумываю над подарком.
bulgarian: One of my sisters has her birthday in a few weeks, so I was trying to decide on a gift.

english: She really likes painting... what do you think I could make her?
french: Elle aime beaucoup peindre... Qu'est-ce que je pourrais lui fabriquer, à ton avis ?
russian: Она любит живопись... Как ты думаешь, что ей смастерить?
bulgarian: She really likes painting... what do you think I could make her?

english: How about some brushes?
french: Pourquoi pas des pinceaux ?
russian: Как насчёт кисточек?
bulgarian: How about some brushes?

english: Maybe a traveling easel?
french: Peut-être un chevalet de voyage ?
russian: Может, походный мольберт?
bulgarian: Maybe a traveling easel?

english: Hey, yeah! That's a good idea, I could do some woodturning and make her something really ergonomic and symmetrical...
french: Mais oui, c'est une très bonne idée ! Avec mon tour à bois, je pourrais lui fabriquer des pinceaux ergonomiques et bien ronds...
russian: О, точно! Это хорошая идея, я могу их как следует обточить, чтобы получилось эргономично и симметрично...
bulgarian: Hey, yeah! That's a good idea, I could do some woodturning and make her something really ergonomic and symmetrical...

english: Maybe break out some of my treasured =Golden Horse Hair= for the bristles!
french: Et je pourrais même utiliser une partie de mon précieux =crin de cheval doré= pour les poils !
russian: Может, даже возьму чуть-чуть своего драгоценного =золотого конского волоса= в качестве щетины.
bulgarian: Maybe break out some of my treasured =Golden Horse Hair= for the bristles!

english: That would be a great gift. Thanks for the idea, [Ari]!
french: Ce serait un super cadeau. Merci pour cette idée, [Ari] !
russian: Будет отличный подарок. Спасибо за идею, [Ari]!
bulgarian: That would be a great gift. Thanks for the idea, [Ari]!

english: Hey, yeah! That's a good idea, maybe one with a pull-out drawer to stow paints?
french: Mais oui, c'est une super idée ! Je pourrais y ajouter un tiroir coulissant pour ranger ses peintures.
russian: О, точно! Это хорошая идея. Может, добавить выдвижной ящичек для красок?
bulgarian: Hey, yeah! That's a good idea, maybe one with a pull-out drawer to stow paints?

english: Maybe I'll ask March to help design the hardware, some nice carrying handles...
french: Je demanderai peut-être à March de fabriquer les éléments métalliques. De jolies poignées de transport par exemple...
russian: Возможно, попрошу Марта сделать металлические части, чтобы ручки были красивые...
bulgarian: Maybe I'll ask March to help design the hardware, some nice carrying handles...

english: That would be a great gift. Thanks for the idea, [Ari]!
french: Ce serait un super cadeau. Merci pour cette idée, [Ari] !
russian: Будет отличный подарок. Спасибо за идею, [Ari]!
bulgarian: That would be a great gift. Thanks for the idea, [Ari]!

english: Oh, hey [Ari]. Can you give me a hand?
french: Oh, [Ari]. Tu veux bien me donner un coup de main ?
russian: О, привет, [Ari]. Можешь помочь?
bulgarian: Oh, hey [Ari]. Can you give me a hand?

english: Uncle Landen snores like crazy.
french: Oncle Landen ronfle comme un sonneur.
russian: Дядя Ланден ужасно храпит.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen snores like crazy.

english: When I first moved in, I thought he was up all night sawing wood, and I was like oh no...
french: Quand je suis arrivé ici, j'ai cru qu'il passait ses nuits à scier du bois et je me suis dit que ce n'était pas possible...
russian: Когда я только приехал, я решил, что он всю ночь пилит брусья, и подумал: «о нет»...
bulgarian: When I first moved in, I thought he was up all night sawing wood, and I was like oh no...

english: But no, it was snoring. He DOES saw wood all day, though. Retired, my left shoe!
french: Mais non, c'est juste qu'il ronfle. Par contre, il passe ses journées à travailler le bois. Retraité, bien sûr...
russian: Но оказалось, что это храп. ЗАТО он пилит брусья целый день! На пенсии он, конечно!
bulgarian: But no, it was snoring. He DOES saw wood all day, though. Retired, my left shoe!

english: Oh no! Did you get used to the noise?
french: Ah mince ! Et tu t'es habitué au bruit ?
russian: О нет! У тебя получилось привыкнуть к шуму?
bulgarian: Oh no! Did you get used to the noise?

english: I wondered about that... he doesn't exactly seem "retired".
french: D'ailleurs, je me demandais... Il n'a pas vraiment l'air à la retraite.
russian: Меня тоже это смущает... Выглядит он не очень пенсионерски, как говорит.
bulgarian: I wondered about that... he doesn't exactly seem "retired".

english: I did, actually.
french: Avec le temps, oui.
russian: Вообще-то, да.
bulgarian: I did, actually.

english: Somehow.
french: En quelque sorte.
russian: Каким-то образом.
bulgarian: Somehow.

english: Mostly...
french: À sa manière...
russian: По большей части...
bulgarian: Mostly...

english: Don't get me started, [Ari].
french: Ne me lance pas sur le sujet, [Ari].
russian: Даже не начинай, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Don't get me started, [Ari].

english: The only thing retirement changed about him is his wardrobe.
french: Le seul changement notable après son départ en retraite, ça a été sa garde-robe.
russian: Всё, что у него изменилось с пенсией, — это гардероб.
bulgarian: The only thing retirement changed about him is his wardrobe.

english: Maybe I should throw him a retirement party... is that what he's waiting for?
french: Je devrais peut-être lui organiser un pot de départ en retraite... Tu crois que c'est ce qu'il attend ?
russian: Может, мне надо устроить ему вечеринку в честь выхода не пенсию... Он этого ждёт?
bulgarian: Maybe I should throw him a retirement party... is that what he's waiting for?

english: [Ari], don't tell him I told you so, but...
french: [Ari], ne lui répète pas, mais...
russian: [Ari], не говори ему, что я жаловался, но...
bulgarian: [Ari], don't tell him I told you so, but...

english: Like, I always admire your sense of style, [Ari]. You're always so yourself, you know?
french: Par exemple, j'adore ton style, [Ari]. Tu es toujours toi-même, si tu vois ce que je veux dire ?
russian: Например, твоё чувство стиля я уважаю, [Ari]. Знаешь, у тебя всегда получается быть собой.
bulgarian: Like, I always admire your sense of style, [Ari]. You're always so yourself, you know?

english: Hit me up if you ever want to talk fashion... it'd be fun to hear your opinions.
french: Viens me voir quand tu veux qu'on discute de mode ! J'adorerais avoir ton point de vue.
russian: Если захочешь обсудить моду, только скажи... Я с радостью послушаю твоё мнение.

english: But you got me thinking about ranching and taking care of animals. I think it'd be fun to learn!

english: You know how my family's bakery is called Ladybird?

french: Tu me plais beaucoup toi aussi.
russian: Ты мне тоже весьма по нраву.
bulgarian: I'm pretty into you, too.

english: That makes me pretty happy, [Ari].
french: Ça me fait plaisir que tu penses ça, [Ari].
russian: Я весьма доволен, [Ari].
bulgarian: That makes me pretty happy, [Ari].

english: Actually, it makes me real happy...
french: En fait, ça me fait énormément plaisir...
russian: Вообще-то, я даже очень доволен...
bulgarian: Actually, it makes me real happy...

english: I'm going to go be... quiet and happy now...
french: Alors, je vais arrêter de parler et je vais savourer ce bonheur.
russian: Пожалуй, лучше я буду... тихо и довольно сидеть.
bulgarian: I'm going to go be... quiet and happy now...

english: I know birding is a weird hobby... a lot of it is about sitting in one place and being quiet.
french: Je sais que l'observation des oiseaux est un loisir étrange... On s'assied quelque part et on attend sans un bruit.
russian: Знаю, наблюдение за птицами — странное хобби... Большую часть времени просто тихо сидишь в одном месте.
bulgarian: I know birding is a weird hobby... a lot of it is about sitting in one place and being quiet.

english: I love the city... I love that it's crowded and loud and you can meet everyone from everywhere.
french: J'adore la ville... la foule, le tohu-bohu et le fait qu'on croise des gens d'un peu partout.
russian: Я люблю город... Люблю крикливые толпы и люблю встречать там самых разных людей.
bulgarian: I love the city... I love that it's crowded and loud and you can meet everyone from everywhere.

english: But I've fallen in love with the country, too. There's so much space here, and it makes space in my head.
french: Mais je suis tombé amoureux de la campagne. Il y a tant d'espace ici. Cela me vide la tête.
russian: Но в это местечко я тоже влюбился. Тут такой простор, и мой разум тоже чувствует себя просторно.
bulgarian: But I've fallen in love with the country, too. There's so much space here, and it makes space in my head.

english: I feel the same way.
french: Je ressens la même chose.
russian: Я чувствую то же самое.
bulgarian: I feel the same way.

english: There's a lot of space on my farm, you know!
french: Il y a beaucoup d'espace aussi dans ma ferme, tu sais !
russian: Знаешь, у меня на ферме тоже очень просторно!
bulgarian: There's a lot of space on my farm, you know!

english: Thought you might.
french: Ça ne m'étonne pas.
russian: Так и думал.
bulgarian: Thought you might.

english: I'm glad you made your way to Mistria and fell in love with it too, [Ari].
french: Je suis content que tu aies choisi Mistria et que tu aimes aussi cet endroit, [Ari].
russian:
Хорошо, что ты

добрались

добраласьдобралсядобралось до Мистрии и тоже

влюбились

влюбиласьвлюбилсявлюбилось в неё, [Ari].
bulgarian: I'm glad you made your way to Mistria and fell in love with it too, [Ari].

english: Wow... we have so much in common...
french: Waouh... On a tant de choses en commun.
russian: Вот это да... Как много у нас общего...
bulgarian: Wow... we have so much in common...

english: Maybe I should ask you out or something?
french: Je devrais peut-être t'inviter à sortir ?
russian: Может, пора пригласить тебя на свидание?
bulgarian: Maybe I should ask you out or something?

english: I should come over some time, get the grand tour.
french: Il faudrait que je vienne à ta ferme... Que tu me fasses faire le tour du propriétaire.
russian: Надо будет как-нибудь зайти к тебе на тур по ферме.
bulgarian: I should come over some time, get the grand tour.

english: Who knows, maybe I'll fall in love with your farm, too.
french: Qui sait ? Je tomberai peut-être amoureux de ta ferme aussi ?!
russian: Кто знает, может, и в неё я тоже влюблюсь.
bulgarian: Who knows, maybe I'll fall in love with your farm, too.

english: I'm glad my dad was never able to talk Uncle Landen into following him to the Capital. It gave me a place to land in Mistria.
french: Je suis content que mon père n'ait jamais réussi à convaincre oncle Landen de s'installer à la capitale. Ça m'a permis d'emménager à Mistria.
russian: Я рад, что отец так и не смог уговорить дядю Ландена поехать с ним в столицу. Благодаря этому у меня есть место в Мистрии.
bulgarian: I'm glad my dad was never able to talk Uncle Landen into following him to the Capital. It gave me a place to land in Mistria.

english: My mom's from a line of bakers, and my dad did deliveries. He brought big sacks of flour to her family's shop every morning.
french: Ma mère vient d'une famille de boulangers et mon père faisait les livraisons. Il leur apportait d'énormes sacs de farine tous les matins.
russian: Моя мать из семьи пекарей, а отец работал разносчиком. По утрам он привозил в лавку её родителей мешки с мукой.
bulgarian: My mom's from a line of bakers, and my dad did deliveries. He brought big sacks of flour to her family's shop every morning.

english: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.
french: La vie est plus simple quand tu grandis en voyant que ça peut être ça, l'amour.
russian: Моя жизнь явно стала лучше с таким примером любви под боком.
bulgarian: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.

english: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back together.
french: C'est peut-être la raison pour laquelle je tenais tant à ce que ce couple de merlebleus de Mistria se retrouve.
russian: Может, поэтому я так увлёкся возвращением мистрийских синешеек.
bulgarian: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back together.

english: And you and I did that together, [Ari].
french: Et c'est ensemble qu'on y est arrivés, [Ari].
russian: И мы с тобой сделали это вместе, [Ari].
bulgarian: And you and I did that together, [Ari].

english: I think... that's pretty romantic, too.
french: Et je trouve ça aussi très romantique.
russian: По-моему... это само по себе довольно романтично.
bulgarian: I think... that's pretty romantic, too.

english: Then one day, mom saw him on the street, and she teased him like, "where's my flour"?
french: Un jour, ma mère le croisa dans la rue et le taquina en lui demandant s'il avait de la fleur de sel.
russian: И однажды она увидела, как он шёл по улице, и стала его дразнить: «А где мешок?»
bulgarian: Then one day, mom saw him on the street, and she teased him like, "where's my flour"?

english: My dad heard it like "flower", and came back with a handful of daisies.
french: Mon père comprit qu'elle voulait des fleurs. Il lui apporta un bouquet de marguerites.
russian: А он услышал «цветок» и вернулся к ней с букетом маргариток.
bulgarian: My dad heard it like "flower", and came back with a handful of daisies.

english: They were inseparable after that. Even when they argue, they do it holding hands.
french: Depuis, ils sont inséparables. Même quand ils se disputent, ils se tiennent la main.
russian: С тех пор они не разлей вода. Даже когда ссорятся, они держатся за руки.
bulgarian: They were inseparable after that. Even when they argue, they do it holding hands.

english: Anyway, just wanted to share. It's nice growing up around a love like that.
french: Enfin, c'était juste pour dire. C'est super de grandir avec tout cet amour.
russian: Ну ладно, это я просто хотел поделиться. Приятно, когда в детстве рядом с тобой такая любовь.
bulgarian: Anyway, just wanted to share. It's nice growing up around a love like that.

english: That's so romantic!
french: C'est tellement romantique !
russian: Как романтично!
bulgarian: That's so romantic!

english: They sound like amazing parents!
french: Ils ont l'air d'être des parents fantastiques !
russian: Кажется, у тебя замечательные родители!
bulgarian: They sound like amazing parents!

english: Yeah, haha... I agree.
french: Ah oui, ha ha ha... c'est vrai.
russian: Да уж, ха-ха... Я согласен.
bulgarian: Yeah, haha... I agree.

english: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.
french: La vie est plus simple quand tu grandis en voyant que ça peut être ça, l'amour.
russian: Моя жизнь явно стала лучше с таким примером любви под боком.
bulgarian: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.

english: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back.
french: C'est peut-être la raison pour laquelle je tenais tant à ce que ce couple de merlebleus de Mistria revienne.
russian: Может, поэтому я так увлёкся возвращением мистрийских синешеек.
bulgarian: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back.

english: They really are.
french: C'est le cas.
russian: Это точно.
bulgarian: They really are.

english: I don't know if I ever mentioned it, but my parents are total lovebirds.
french: Je ne sais pas si je te l'ai déjà dit, mais mes parents sont amoureux comme au premier jour.
russian: По-моему, я тебе ещё не рассказывал: мои родители ужасно романтичные.
bulgarian: I don't know if I ever mentioned it, but my parents are total lovebirds.

english: But I definitely started crushing on you at some point.
french: Mais je suis clairement tombé amoureux.
russian: Но в какой-то момент я точно стал в тебя влюбляться.
bulgarian: But I definitely started crushing on you at some point.

english: Who wouldn't, if they saw you persevering like that literally every day...
french: Qui aurait pu résister en te voyant te donner à fond jour après jour...?
russian: Я видел, как ты усердно трудишься буквально каждый день — кто бы тут устоял...
bulgarian: Who wouldn't, if they saw you persevering like that literally every day...

english: Anyway, I'm glad my crush panned out.
french: Toujours est-il que je suis content que tu partages mes sentiments.
russian: И как я рад, что моя влюблённость не односторонняя.
bulgarian: Anyway, I'm glad my crush panned out.

english: We worked side-by-side to restore the town for so long, and I don't know when it was...
french: On travaille ensemble à la reconstruction de la ville depuis très longtemps et je ne sais plus quand c'était...
russian: Мы так долго работали над восстановлением города рука об руку, что я даже не знаю, когда это началось...
bulgarian: We worked side-by-side to restore the town for so long, and I don't know when it was...

english: You look cute today.
french: Tu es à croquer aujourd'hui.
russian: Мило выглядишь сегодня.
bulgarian: You look cute today.

english: Hey...
french: Hé...
russian: Эй...
bulgarian: Hey...

english: It's good, right?
french: Il n'est pas mauvais, hein ?
russian: Вкусно, правда?
bulgarian: It's good, right?

english: You know...
french: Tu sais...
russian: Знаешь...
bulgarian: You know...

english: If my sisters were here, they'd be teasing us that sharing a straw is an indirect kiss.
french: Si mes sœurs étaient là, elles nous diraient que partager une paille, c'est une manière de s'embrasser.
russian: Если бы здесь были мои сёстры, они бы дразнились, что у нас непрямой поцелуй через соломинку.
bulgarian: If my sisters were here, they'd be teasing us that sharing a straw is an indirect kiss.

english: I won't tell them if you don't.
french: Mais je ne leur dirai rien.
russian: Но мы им не будем рассказывать, хорошо?
bulgarian: I won't tell them if you don't.

english: I was just trying some new cold brew... want a sip?
french: J'allais goûter un nouveau café infusé à froid. Tu en veux ?
russian: Я тут попробовал новый кофе холодной заварки... Хочешь глотнуть?
bulgarian: I was just trying some new cold brew... want a sip?

english: It was more like a pond, though.
french: C'était plus un étang qu'un lac, d'ailleurs.
russian: Правда, это, скорее, пруд.
bulgarian: It was more like a pond, though.

english: There's a pond by the manor. Just saying, we should go some time.
french: Il y a un étang près du manoir. On pourrait y aller un de ces jours.
russian: А здесь есть пруд около особняка. Просто предлагаю: можем как-нибудь сходить.
bulgarian: There's a pond by the manor. Just saying, we should go some time.

english: Back in the Capital there was a park, and in the park there was Lover's Lake.
french: À la capitale, il y avait un parc avec un lac appelé le lac des Amoureux.
russian: Там, в столице, есть парк, а в нём есть Озеро любовников.
bulgarian: Back in the Capital there was a park, and in the park there was Lover's Lake.

english: But now, whenever I see you... I feel really really good about it.
french: Mais maintenant, quand je te vois... je suis encore plus content.
russian: А теперь, когда я вижу тебя... Я очень-очень рад, что переехал.
bulgarian: But now, whenever I see you... I feel really really good about it.

english: Gotta say... I already felt good about moving here to take on the apprenticeship with Uncle Landen.
french: Tu sais... J'étais content d'avoir emménagé ici pour faire mon apprentissage avec oncle Landen.
russian: Должен тебе сказать... Я и так был рад переехать сюда, чтобы поучиться у дяди Ландена.
bulgarian: Gotta say... I already felt good about moving here to take on the apprenticeship with Uncle Landen.

english: Just saying.
french: Je dis ça comme ça...
russian: Это так, к слову.
bulgarian: Just saying.

english: You know... I'd totally share a birdhouse with you.
french: Tu sais, ça me dirait bien de partager un petit nid d'amour avec toi.
russian: Ты знаешь... Я бы точно поселился с тобой в одном скворечнике.
bulgarian: You know... I'd totally share a birdhouse with you.

english: He was super excited, talking about how he knew all along.
french: Il est ravi et il n'a pas arrêté de dire qu'il l'avait senti venir.
russian: Он так обрадовался и стал говорить, что всегда это знал.
bulgarian: He was super excited, talking about how he knew all along.

english: It was nice, so I wanted to tell you. But also warn you.
french: J'ai trouvé ça adorable, alors je voulais te le dire. Mais aussi te prévenir.
russian: Это было очень мило, так что я захотел тебе рассказать. Но и предупредить тоже.
bulgarian: It was nice, so I wanted to tell you. But also warn you.

english: You know how my uncle is.
french: Tu connais mon oncle...
russian: Ты же знаешь моего дядю.
bulgarian: You know how my uncle is.

english: Uncle Landen finally figured out that you and I have something going on.
french: Oncle Landen a enfin compris qu'il se passait quelque chose entre nous.
russian: Дядя Ланден наконец прознал, что у нас с тобой что-то есть.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen finally figured out that you and I have something going on.

english: Greetings, [Ari].
french: Je te salue, [Ari].
russian: Приветствую, [Ari].
bulgarian: Greetings, [Ari].

english: Yes? Did you need something, [Ari]?
french: Oui ? As-tu besoin de quelque chose, [Ari] ?
russian: Да? Тебе что-то нужно, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Yes? Did you need something, [Ari]?

english: Juniper sets the ambiance well.
french: Juniper sait créer une ambiance.
russian: Джунипер умеет создать правильную атмосферу.
bulgarian: Juniper sets the ambiance well.

english: The aromas that fill this bathhouse... they are invigorating.
french: Les arômes qui emplissent ces bains... Ils sont revigorants.
russian: Ароматы в этой купальне... помогают взбодриться.
bulgarian: The aromas that fill this bathhouse... they are invigorating.

english: What? It is a figure of speech.
french: Qu'y a-t-il ? C'est juste une façon de parler.
russian: Что? Это просто фигура речи.
bulgarian: What? It is a figure of speech.

english: Oh, this bathhouse is a luxury worth killing for.
french: Oh ! Je pourrais tuer pour savourer le luxe de ces bains.
russian: О, за такую роскошь, как эта купальня, я готова убить.
bulgarian: Oh, this bathhouse is a luxury worth killing for.

english: I will have a word with Dozy about it.
french: Il faudra que j'en parle à Dozy.
russian: Надо будет обсудить это с Дрёмой.
bulgarian: I will have a word with Dozy about it.

english: Try as I might, the bins in the changing room are not big enough to hold my armor...
french: J'ai beau essayer, les paniers à disposition dans les vestiaires ne sont pas assez grands pour contenir mon armure.
russian: Мои доспехи не вмещаются в корзины в раздевалке, как бы я ни старалась...
bulgarian: Try as I might, the bins in the changing room are not big enough to hold my armor...

english: I never did find a hot spring large enough to accommodate my draconic form.
french: Je ne suis jamais parvenue à trouver une source chaude assez vaste pour accueillir ma forme de dragon.
russian: В драконьем обличье мне так и не удалось отыскать горячий источник подходящего размера.
bulgarian: I never did find a hot spring large enough to accommodate my draconic form.

english: It is a pleasure to enjoy a hot bath in a mortal body.
french: C'est un plaisir de savourer un bain chaud dans un corps mortel.
russian: В теле смертного очень приятно принимать горячую ванну.
bulgarian: It is a pleasure to enjoy a hot bath in a mortal body.

english: I will make accommodations for her feelings. For now.
french: Je vais prendre en compte son ressenti. Pour l'instant.
russian: Пожалуй, я проявлю уважение к её чувствам. На сей раз.
bulgarian: I will make accommodations for her feelings. For now.

english: But perhaps, once she is distracted...
french: Mais peut-être qu'un jour où elle sera distraite...
russian: Но, возможно, когда она отвлечётся...
bulgarian: But perhaps, once she is distracted...

english: I came here to wash my armor in the magic-infused water of this bathhouse... but it seems Juniper is against such things.
french: Je suis venue ici pour laver mon armure dans les eaux imprégnées de magie de ces bains... mais Juniper y semble opposée.
russian: Я хотела омыть свои доспехи в богатых магией водах этой купальни... Но оказалось, что Джунипер это не по нраву.
bulgarian: I came here to wash my armor in the magic-infused water of this bathhouse... but it seems Juniper is against such things.

english: But as a dragon, I wouldn't mind if the water was a few hundred degrees hotter.
french: Mais en tant que dragon, il ne me déplairait pas que cette eau ait quelques centaines de degrés de plus.
russian: Но, будучи драконом, я была бы не прочь сделать на сто-двести градусов погорячее.
bulgarian: But as a dragon, I wouldn't mind if the water was a few hundred degrees hotter.

english: The temperature of the baths is pleasant enough...
french: La température de ces bains est assez plaisante...
russian: Температура воды в купальне достаточно приятна...
bulgarian: The temperature of the baths is pleasant enough...

english: Long ago, I wished to test my mettle against the strongest foes I could find. And so, I followed the peculiar tale of a terrifying sea beast to the source.
french: Il y a fort longtemps, j'ai voulu me mesurer aux ennemis les plus redoutables. J'ai donc tenté de retrouver une créature marine légendaire et terrifiante.
russian: Когда-то давно я решила померяться силами с самыми грозными противниками. Тогда я отыскала источник занимательных рассказов про ужасное морское чудище.
bulgarian: Long ago, I wished to test my mettle against the strongest foes I could find. And so, I followed the peculiar tale of a terrifying sea beast to the source.

english: What I found was a shark, of a bloodthirsty ferocity that impressed even me. It sensed in me a fellow predator, and charged without hesitation.
french: J'ai découvert un requin d'une férocité sanguinaire, impressionnante même pour moi. Il a senti en moi un prédateur rival et m'a chargée sans hésiter.
russian: И нашла акулу, которая привела меня в восторг своей свирепостью и кровожадностью. Она сразу учуяла во мне собрата-хищника и бесстрашно понеслесь мне навстречу.
bulgarian: What I found was a shark, of a bloodthirsty ferocity that impressed even me. It sensed in me a fellow predator, and charged without hesitation.

english: We fought for three days and nights, and in the end, I emerged victorious. I took its mighty cartilaginous jaw and preserved it as my trophy...
french: Nous avons combattu trois jours et trois nuits et j'ai fini par l'emporter. J'ai conservé en trophée sa puissante mâchoire cartilagineuse...
russian: Мы сражались три дня и три ночи, и наконец я одержала победу. Я вырезала её могучий челюстной хрящ и забрала в качестве трофея...
bulgarian: We fought for three days and nights, and in the end, I emerged victorious. I took its mighty cartilaginous jaw and preserved it as my trophy...

english: And that is the story of how I came to possess my swim attire.
french: Et c'est ainsi que j'ai obtenu ce qui me sert aujourd'hui de maillot de bain.
russian: Вот так у меня и появился купальник.
bulgarian: And that is the story of how I came to possess my swim attire.

english: I have a story to tell you, [Ari].
french: J'ai une histoire à te raconter, [Ari].
russian: Расскажу тебе одну историю, [Ari].
bulgarian: I have a story to tell you, [Ari].

english: If you explore deep enough, it becomes quiet and dark as night. The fish glow like little stars.
french: Lorsqu'on plonge assez profondément, tout devient noir et silencieux comme la nuit. Les poissons brillent, telles de petites étoiles.
russian: Если зайти вдаль от берега, он становится тихий и тёмный, словно сама ночь. А рыбы мерцают, как звёздочки.
bulgarian: If you explore deep enough, it becomes quiet and dark as night. The fish glow like little stars.

english: Night above, and below... the thought pleases me.
french: La nuit, au-dessus et en dessous... Cette idée me plaît.
russian: Ночь наверху и ночь подо мной... Это приятное чувство.
bulgarian: Night above, and below... the thought pleases me.

english: I am partial to the ocean.
french: J'ai un faible pour l'océan.
russian: Я питаю слабость к океану.
bulgarian: I am partial to the ocean.

english: And then, as though to bolster its defiance, it pinched me again.
french: Et puis, comme pour appuyer son attitude de défi, il m'a pincée à nouveau.
russian: А затем ущипнул ещё раз, с удвоенной дерзостью.
bulgarian: And then, as though to bolster its defiance, it pinched me again.

english: I admire such pluck. Yes... that little crab will go far.
french: J'admire une telle audace. Oui... Ce petit crabe ira loin.
russian: Я поощряю такую отвагу. Да... У маленького краба большое будущее.
bulgarian: I admire such pluck. Yes... that little crab will go far.

english: I was walking along the shore when a little crab pinched me.
french: Je marchais le long du rivage quand un petit crabe m'a pincée.
russian: Я прогуливалась вдоль берега, как вдруг меня ущипнул краб.
bulgarian: I was walking along the shore when a little crab pinched me.

english: It pleases me to view this idyllic scene...
french: Il me plaît de contempler ce paysage idyllique...
russian: Мне нравится наблюдать за этим безмятежным пейзажем...
bulgarian: It pleases me to view this idyllic scene...

english: Waiting for the illusion to shatter when a mighty sea monster rears its head to challenge me.
french: Et d'attendre que l'illusion se brise quand un puissant monstre marin se dressera pour me défier.
russian: И ждать, когда эта иллюзия рухнет и могучее морское чудовище поднимет голову из глубин, бросая мне вызов.
bulgarian: Waiting for the illusion to shatter when a mighty sea monster rears its head to challenge me.

english: But do not worry. I will fell any foe that dares to approach.
french: Mais ne t'inquiète pas. Je vaincrai n'importe quel ennemi qui aura l'audace d'approcher.
russian: Только не переживай. Я сражу любого, кто пойдёт мне навстречу.
bulgarian: But do not worry. I will fell any foe that dares to approach.

english: Like now! Look there!
french: Comme là ! Regarde !
russian: Вон, смотри! Вот там!
bulgarian: Like now! Look there!

english: Ah. It is just more driftwood. What a shame.
french: Ah. Ce n'est que du bois flotté. Quel dommage !
russian: А, опять коряга. Какая жалость.
bulgarian: Ah. It is just more driftwood. What a shame.

english: Would you like to watch the waves with me, [Ari]?
french: Aimerais-tu regarder les vagues avec moi, [Ari] ?
russian: Ты желаешь понаблюдать за волнами со мной, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Would you like to watch the waves with me, [Ari]?

english: Such a gesture is unnecessary... I prefer to use my claws when hunting.
french: Ce genre de geste n'est pas nécessaire... Je préfère utiliser mes griffes pour la chasse.
russian: Напрасная щедрость... Я предпочитаю охотиться с помощью когтей.
bulgarian: Such a gesture is unnecessary... I prefer to use my claws when hunting.

english: Terithia saw me stalking along the water's edge and offered me one of her fishing rods.
french: Terithia m'a vue rôder au bord de l'eau et m'a proposé l'une de ses cannes à pêche.
russian: Теризия увидела, как я брожу возле воды, и предложила мне свою удочку.
bulgarian: Terithia saw me stalking along the water's edge and offered me one of her fishing rods.

english: A place with an embrace beyond all limits, where a mortal body would surely shatter.
french: Un endroit dont l'étreinte ne connaît aucune limite, où un corps mortel serait sûrement brisé.
russian: Океан там сжимает со всех сторон, будто в крепких объятиях, от которых бы раздробилось тело любого смертного.
bulgarian: A place with an embrace beyond all limits, where a mortal body would surely shatter.

english: To a dragon, it is like a sanctuary. Deathly...
french: Pour un dragon, ce serait là un sanctuaire. Fatal...
russian: Для дракона это заповедное место. Смертельно опасное...
bulgarian: To a dragon, it is like a sanctuary. Deathly...

english: And thus, peaceful.
french: Et par conséquent, paisible.
russian: И потому спокойное.
bulgarian: And thus, peaceful.

english: Deep in the ocean, there is a place that no light can reach.
french: Au plus profond de l'océan se trouve un lieu que la lumière ne peut atteindre.
russian: В глубине океана есть место, куда не достигает свет.
bulgarian: Deep in the ocean, there is a place that no light can reach.

english: But it has been countless ages since that time.
french: Mais bien des lustres se sont écoulés depuis lors.
russian: Но с тех пор прошли несчётные столетия.
bulgarian: But it has been countless ages since that time.

english: I wonder... What remains from that era?
french: Que reste-t-il de cette époque ? Je me le demande.
russian: Интересно... Что сохранилось с той эпохи?
bulgarian: I wonder... What remains from that era?

english: And what must I teach mortals anew?
french: Et que dois-je à nouveau enseigner aux mortels ?
russian: И чему мне следует учить смертных вновь?
bulgarian: And what must I teach mortals anew?

english: I was once worshipped as a goddess in this land.
french: J'étais jadis vénérée comme une déesse sur ces terres.
russian: Когда-то в этих землях меня почитали как богиню.
bulgarian: I was once worshipped as a goddess in this land.

english: Look! The myriad colors of fruit rival that of my glittering hoard.
french: Regarde ! La myriade de couleurs de ces fruits rivalise avec mes richesses scintillantes.
russian: Взгляни! Плоды переливаются мириадами красок, словно лучшие из моих сокровищ.
bulgarian: Look! The myriad colors of fruit rival that of my glittering hoard.

english: The variety of foods this little store is able to stock is impressive.
french: La diversité d'aliments que cette petite boutique a en réserve est impressionnante.
russian: Этот маленький магазинчик обеспечивает поистине впечатляющее разнообразие пищи.
bulgarian: The variety of foods this little store is able to stock is impressive.

english: It is like watching an anthill inside of a jar.
french: C'est comme contempler une fourmilière dans un bocal.
russian: Это как наблюдать за муравьиной кучей в банке.
bulgarian: It is like watching an anthill inside of a jar.

english: It delights me, the bustle of mortals going about their daily lives.
french: L'agitation des mortels vaquant à leurs occupations me réjouit.
russian: Мне нравится наблюдать, как смертные суетятся изо дня в день.
bulgarian: It delights me, the bustle of mortals going about their daily lives.

english: Perhaps I should practice my new spells in the village square.
french: Je devrais peut-être m'entraîner à mes nouveaux sorts sur la place du village.
russian: Может, мне стоит испытать мои новые заклинания на главной площади.
bulgarian: Perhaps I should practice my new spells in the village square.

english: It would certainly liven things up.
french: Cela mettrait sans aucun doute de l'animation.
russian: Это точно их взбодрит.
bulgarian: It would certainly liven things up.

english: Sometimes I look around and think these townsfolk have become too complacent.
french: Parfois, je regarde autour de moi et je me dis que ces villageois sont devenus bien trop insouciants.
russian: Иногда я смотрю вокруг и думаю, что местные жители слишком расслабились.
bulgarian: Sometimes I look around and think these townsfolk have become too complacent.

english: Time is cyclical, and our reign of fire will surely burn again.
french: Le temps s'écoule de manière cyclique et notre règne de feu brûlera de nouveau un jour.
russian: Время идёт по кругу. Когда-нибудь наше огненное царство обязательно разгорится вновь.
bulgarian: Time is cyclical, and our reign of fire will surely burn again.

english: The age of dragons may have passed, but do not fret.
french: L'époque des dragons est révolue, mais ne t'inquiète pas.
russian: Времена драконов прошли, но не предавайся отчаянию.
bulgarian: The age of dragons may have passed, but do not fret.

english: We should do as we did in my youth...
french: Nous devrions faire comme au temps de ma jeunesse...
russian: Надо попробовать развлечься, как в молодости...
bulgarian: We should do as we did in my youth...

english: Single out the brawniest mortals and make them fight for our entertainment.
french: Distinguer les mortels les plus combatifs et les faire s'affronter pour notre divertissement.
russian: Выбрать самых крепких смертных и заставить их сражаться нам на потеху.
bulgarian: Single out the brawniest mortals and make them fight for our entertainment.

english: Then the winner will have the honor of fighting me.
french: Le vainqueur aurait ensuite l'honneur de se battre contre moi.
russian: А победитель заслужит честь сражаться со мной.
bulgarian: Then the winner will have the honor of fighting me.

english: What do you say, [Ari]?
french: Qu'en dis-tu, [Ari] ?
russian: Что скажешь, [Ari]?
bulgarian: What do you say, [Ari]?

english: Today, I find myself feeling listless.
french: Je me sens apathique, aujourd'hui.
russian: Сегодня я чувствую необыкновенное утомление.
bulgarian: Today, I find myself feeling listless.

english: It is a mode of expression that I favor.
french: C'est un mode d'expression que je privilégie.
russian: Для меня это наиболее привычный способ самовыражения.
bulgarian: It is a mode of expression that I favor.

english: Perhaps you and I can bring it back into fashion.
french: Peut-être que toi et moi, nous pourrions le remettre à la mode.
russian: Возможно, вместе у нас получится вернуть его в моду.
bulgarian: Perhaps you and I can bring it back into fashion.

english: I am surprised the people of this era do not wear the bones of their enemies.
french: Je suis surprise que le peuple de cette époque n'arbore pas les os de ses ennemis.
russian: Я удивлена, что люди в эту эпоху не носят кости своих врагов.
bulgarian: I am surprised the people of this era do not wear the bones of their enemies.

english: But fear not... they will be reborn as $Rose Hips$ with the coming of winter.
french: Mais n'aie crainte... Elles renaîtront sous la forme d'$églantines$ à l'arrivée de l'hiver.
russian: Но не бойся... Когда придёт зима, они переродятся в $шиповник$.
bulgarian: But fear not... they will be reborn as $Rose Hips$ with the coming of winter.

english: Such is the cycle of death and rebirth.
french: Tel est le cycle de la mort et de la renaissance.
russian: Таковы законы жизни и смерти.
bulgarian: Such is the cycle of death and rebirth.

english: I see the $Roses$ withered at the end of summer...
french: Je constate que les $roses$ ont fané à la fin de l'été...
russian: Я видела, как в конце лета увяли $розы$...
bulgarian: I see the $Roses$ withered at the end of summer...

english: Gazing upon this manor garden, I can see that Celine has been successful in finding her path in this lifetime.
french: Quand je contemple le jardin de ce manoir, je constate que Céline est parvenue à trouver sa voie dans l'existence.
russian: Присмотревшись к саду особняка, я отмечаю, что Селин удалось найти свой путь в этой жизни.
bulgarian: Gazing upon this manor garden, I can see that Celine has been successful in finding her path in this lifetime.

english: I wonder what she might accomplish, if she turned her eye to destruction rather than creation...
french: Je me demande de quoi elle serait capable si elle se tournait vers la destruction, plutôt que la création...
russian: Интересно, каких высот она смогла бы достичь, если бы обратила свои таланты на разрушение, а не на созидание...
bulgarian: I wonder what she might accomplish, if she turned her eye to destruction rather than creation...

english: Such a thought amuses me.
french: Cette pensée m'amuse.
russian: Мне занимательно об этом размышлять.
bulgarian: Such a thought amuses me.

english: Interesting...
french: C'est intéressant...
russian: Любопытно...
bulgarian: Interesting...

english: Each inhabitant has its own needs and demands.
french: Chaque habitant a des besoins et des exigences qui lui sont propres.
russian: У каждого обитателя свои желания и потребности.
bulgarian: Each inhabitant has its own needs and demands.

english: I ruled my own kingdoms to great success for eons...
french: J'ai dirigé mes royaumes avec grand succès pendant des siècles...
russian: Я управляла своими королевствами многие тысячелетия — и с большим успехом...
bulgarian: I ruled my own kingdoms to great success for eons...

english: But unfortunately, plants seem to wither at my touch.
french: Mais malheureusement, les plantes semblent dépérir quand je les touche.
russian: Но, к сожалению, растения увядают, когда я их касаюсь.
bulgarian: But unfortunately, plants seem to wither at my touch.

english: Managing a garden is like managing a kingdom...
french: La gestion d'un jardin est semblable à celle d'un royaume...
russian: Следить за садом — всё равно что следить за королевством...
bulgarian: Managing a garden is like managing a kingdom...

english: And soon, the pretty flowers in this garden will succumb to the frosts of winter.
french: Et bientôt, les jolies fleurs de ce jardin succomberont aux gelées de l'hiver.
russian: Скоро прелестные цветы в этом саду падут перед зимними холодами.
bulgarian: And soon, the pretty flowers in this garden will succumb to the frosts of winter.

english: In death, they will nurture what comes after.
french: Dans la mort, elles nourriront ce qui viendra après elles.
russian: И их смерть подготовит почву для тех, кто придёт после них.
bulgarian: In death, they will nurture what comes after.

english: Endings always serve a purpose, you see.
french: Une fin sert toujours un but, vois-tu.
russian: Как видишь, окончание — всегда лишь шаг к новой цели.
bulgarian: Endings always serve a purpose, you see.

english: The air becomes sharp with cold...
french: L'air froid devient piquant...
russian: В воздухе уже чувствуется колючий мороз...
bulgarian: The air becomes sharp with cold...

english: There is no need to actually feed villagers to the fish... but the thought of it is enough to keep subjects in line.
french: Nul besoin de nourrir ces poissons avec des habitants... mais cette perspective suffit généralement à rendre des sujets dociles.
russian: Местных жителей вовсе не обязательно отправлять им на корм... Но эта мысль поможет держать их в повиновении.
bulgarian: There is no need to actually feed villagers to the fish... but the thought of it is enough to keep subjects in line.

english: I am not certain she took my proposal seriously...
french: Je ne suis pas certaine qu'elle ait pris ma proposition au sérieux.
russian: Я не уверена, что она восприняла моё предложение всерьёз.
bulgarian: I am not certain she took my proposal seriously...

english: I suggested to Adeline to add some man-eating fish to the manor pond.
french: J'ai suggéré à Adeline d'ajouter des poissons mangeurs d'hommes dans l'étang du manoir.
russian: Я предложила Аделине добавить в пруд возле особняка рыб-людоедов.
bulgarian: I suggested to Adeline to add some man-eating fish to the manor pond.
